ResponsesInList.Title: Anyone know of any Projected Grade Plugins?
ResponsesInList.Text: Maybe it has something to do with whether you are a right-brain or left-brain person???🧠 In my courses, I never told students how many graded items the course contained. This gave me the ability to change my mind. There were a few situations where students might want to do this calculation. 1) At the end of the course, before they took their final exam. 2) During a semester, when a student wondered how much they should argue for more points on an assignment. I found that less than .5% of the students would ask for this feature. For me, the instructor, I would do a little "what if" to decide if a student very short of a grade boundary should be moved up, such as a student getting a 92.92, when an "A" would be 93.  But I would only mention this small adjustment near the end of the semester. ResponsesInList.Title: Anyone know of any Projected Grade Plugins?
ResponsesInList.Text: I did the same thing as Canvas projected grades, but with Moodle and a sheet of paper. I did this for fifteen years and it was very motivating, so I support doing a more automated approach on Moodle. On the paper, students would make a list of every graded part of the course, with points totalling 100. They then would keep adding the grades to the list as they go in the course and multiply by the percentage of that assignment. They could estimate their grade manually--it was good math practice too. . Result: more students did all the assignments, and more students got "A"s because grades were not on a curve--but based on effort and qualitative rubrics for performance projects.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recalculating grades after upgrading Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, The behaviour described was introduced in https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-75878 to improve the grade recalculation process triggered when a new gradable activity is created. This update specifically targets large courses, which were most affected by the previous method. Previously, the activity creation and grade recalculation occurred in the same request. In large courses, this recalculation could take a significant amount of time and sometimes result in a time-out, causing the activity creation to fail as well. Now, when a new gradable activity is created, a check is performed to determine if the recalculation process will be time-consuming - currently defined as courses with more than 100 grades. In such cases, the recalculation is handled in a separate request with a progress bar displayed. While the overall waiting time remains the same, this approach prevents users from being blocked from creating activities if the recalculation times out. For courses with fewer than 100 grades, the original approach - processing everything within a single request is still used. This explains the discrepancy in behaviour between different courses. I hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Advanced grade item options ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear All, As we upgrade from Moodle 4.3 to 4.5, I've noticed that there are no more "Advanced" check boxes on the "Grade category settings" page (/admin/settings.php?section=gradecategorysettings). This puzzled me because the Moodle docs page mentions them, as ever before:  cf. https://docs.moodle.org/405/en/Grade_category_settings ("The "Advanced" checkbox will hide the specific feature until the "Show advanced" button is used by the teacher. This will reduce initial menu choices for teachers but allow them to see them if they wish. ") I started investigating and noticed that the "Advanced grade item options" (grade_item_advanced) section and drop-down on the /admin/settings.php?section=gradeitemsettings page ("Grade item settings") was also missing... There was no mention of any sensible kind in the moodle.org or moodledev.io domains, so I searched wildly for "grade_item_advanced" across the entire internet, which gave me this hit that gave me a lead: https://moodle.schomburg-chemie.de/admin/upgrade.txt where I read at the top: "This files describes API changes in /admin/*. === 4.4 === * Grade item setting "Advanced grade item options" (grade_item_advanced) is no longer used and has been removed. * Grade category settings no longer have the "Advanced" checkbox. The 'advanced' parameter has been removed. " I then found the same lines in my local Windows install of Moodle 4.4 in the file \ server \moodle\admin\upgrade.txt . And this is how I learned that the feature had been REMOVED with Moodle 4.4 arriving in April 2024. But there seems to have been NO real mention of that change anywhere. This page https://moodledev.io/general/releases/4.4 is silent (none of the listed tracker issues corresponds to the change). And silent are also the Moodle doc's. My focused Google search would have captured a relevant Moodle Tracker page, I believe? Well, no I had to go the Tracker and search for grade_item_advanced there to locate https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-78967 ("Remove unused advanced grade item/category settings"), which I had not been aware of. My bad, but... not completely IMO . Now, I'd been used to controlling what would show at once and what was an "Advanced option" of an "Edit grade" page. One of my favourite fields to show at once was "Grade to pass". And actually I have only noticed this now that also in Moodle 4.3 it fails to show at once - since there's the initial modal popup for editing a grade item, offers a single link for "Show more". No more "Show advanced" handles (that change I do remember following, true). Ergo, grade_item_advanced has been ignored by Moodle 4.3.* for quite some time, apparently. It dawns on me, on the basis all this experience, that my admin preferences for "Advanced" will be completely gone after I upgrade from Moodle 43 to 45; and the "Edit grade" will look the same for all, with only these pre-selected fields to show on first click: Item name, Grade type, Maximum grade, Minimum grade, Hidden Locked, Weight adjusted, Extra credit. My fav "Grade to pass" is not on this list, and there is no admin option available to make it show :/ Or maybe there IS a (new?) way to control the contents of the "Edit grade" initial pop-up? Regardless if an answer to my question above can be positive or not, I believe suitable updates are needed to these docs to acknowledge the work done in https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-78967: https://docs.moodle.org/405/en/Grade_items#Advanced_grade_item_options https://docs.moodle.org/404/en/Grade_items#Advanced_grade_item_options https://docs.moodle.org/405/en/Grade_category_settings https://docs.moodle.org/404/en/Grade_category_settings as well as to the Moodle 4.4 release notes: https://moodledev.io/general/releases/4.4 Unless I'm getting something wrong here... With kind regards, Przemek

ResponsesInList.Title: USing Scales and Rubrics Together
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I have an instructor who is looking to use rubrics and scales together. Her rubric has 5 criteria with three  point levels: 0, 1, 2. (So maximum possible points would be 10) However, wants to use a Met/Revise scale so Met is "100%" and Revise is "0%". She was trying to see if she could set it up so that if a student scores a perfect 10 on the rubric it is "Met" but if they score anything less than that it is a "Revise" The only way I can see this working is if she creates a scale with levels that correspond to her rubric. So, if she has 11 possible scores in the rubric (0/10, 1/10, 2/10, 3/10, 4/10, 5/10, 6/10, 7/10, 8/10, 9/10, 10/10)  she will need to create a scale that does the same: Revise 0/10, Revise 1/10, Revise 2/10, and so on until you get to "Met" which would be 10/10.. It is not as neat and tidy as she is hoping, but it does seem to work . But is also makes the grade item have a maximum grade of 11 points rather than a maximum grade of 2 points if she were using her Met/Revise scale. I was looking for any thoughts or ideas or if this is just not even possible given the way that scales and rubrics work on their own. I was also playing with the Offset setting for the grade with the idea that I could offset grade that the rubric is calculating with a negative value so it matched the Met/Revise scale's all or nothing grading. For example, if a perfect score is 10 and anything less is 0, then I tried making the offset number -9. But that didn't do anything and I'm not even sure if I'm using this correctly or barking up the wrong tree. Any thoughts appreciated. But I'm assuming this is not possible. Thanks! Marybeth

For example: the Maximum Grade for an Essay Question is 5.55, which represents three separate elements, such as Alignment, Desire, and Availability.  These three elements are each graded on a scale of 1-5.  Thus, a grade value of 4.35 would represent the 3-part grade of: Alignment = 4/5 Desire = 3/5 Availability = 5/5 We like how this is instantly informative visually, instead of using Scales to calculate a combined score that requires further explanation.  However, it causes a decreasing level of importance for each element, which clearly isn't ideal for calculating the Quiz's final grade total.  Only using whole numbers creates other issues, like extremely large question values and relative weight problems.  We're also not sure if we're actually just complicating things with our limited understanding of grading. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to make an assignment extra credit without using simple weighted mean of grades?

ResponsesInList.Title: Option to Exclude Hidden Items from Grader Report Grade Calculation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I’ve noticed that unlike the User Report, our Grader Report doesn’t have an option to exclude hidden items from the total grade calculation. As you can see below, the User Report gives the option of excluding hidden items from overall grades-- (this is the "View as User" option). Could we get a similar option for the Grader Report? Perhaps we could call it "Include hidden items in calculations" or "do not include hidden items in calculations". This feature would really help streamline the grading process, especially since I have all my (hundreds of) items nicely organized and categorized chronologically. Right now, the only workaround is for me to shuffle activities into a "non-graded" category and move them to their appropriate graded categories as they're opened. However, this becomes quite a mess as I handle about 20 small activities each week and they don’t always stay in order when moved. It would be so much simpler to just unhide them and have them slot into place automatically. Furthermore, seeing an activity or a quiz automatically count against a student's grade motivates them to complete it as fast as possible. Finally, when it comes time to calculate final grades, it would be incredibly helpful to have a total that accurately reflects only the visible grades. Is it possible to add this feature to the Grader Report? It would make a huge difference for those of us with a lot of activities to manage. Thanks for considering this improvement!

ResponsesInList.Title: Option to Exclude Hidden Items from Grader Report Grade Calculation
ResponsesInList.Text: This 'should' be the setting found in Grades - Setup - Course Grade Settings -- "Hide totals if they contain hidden items" setting with "Show totals excluding hidden items" selected for that setting. Edit: I just realized at the top of that settings page: " Course grade settings determine how the gradebook appears for all participants in the course. " Followup - If the hidden items are simply future items not yet completed by the user, maybe try using the "Exclude empty grades" option in the Gradebook Setup so it only counts graded activities. I've not utilized the "Hidden until..." setting on each activity on the Setup page to see if that hides the activity from calculation from just the student or both student & teacher...

I'd like this option to also affect the Grader Report, or at least have a way of toggling it on the Grader Report. The problem with using "Exclude Empty Grades" is that if that any unhidden assignments that are not completed by a student count as 100%. So, if a student has one assignment done with 100% and 9 open assignments that have not been attempted, his grade would show up as 100%, which is not what I would want. Also, I end up opening only around 30% of the hundreds of hidden activities I have in certain categories-- depending on the semester. Moving these from one category to another is infeasible. Clarification: Most of my assignments are actually "quiz" activities that are auto-graded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Option to Exclude Hidden Items from Grader Report Grade Calculation
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for pointing out the complexities involved with the interactions between hidden/unhidden items, and excluded/included grades. I've gone ahead and created a tracker request to address these issues more systematically. This was my first time using the tracker request system; I wish I had known about it earlier! In the meantime, I've developed a workaround that might help simplify the grade viewing process, even for those without administrator access. You can suggest this to your administrator if you yourself don't have administrative rights: Create a "Grader View" Role: This role is based on the "Non-editing teacher" but set to prevent viewing hidden grades. This allows anyone in this role to see the grader report exactly as students would, without the hidden items affecting the total. Allow Role Switching: Ensure that teachers can switch to the "Grader View" role from their normal teaching role. This switch can be easily done from the user menu and doesn't require role assignment at the course level. As for exporting the grader report with accurate course totals, a quick workaround I found effective is to simply use 'Control + A' (Cmd + A on Mac) to select all content on the grader report screen, and then paste it as plain text into an Excel sheet. This method has been working well for me since the normal report export feature messes up the course totals. I hope these steps help alleviate some of the issues many of us have been experiencing until a more permanent fix can be implemented through the tracker system. Below is a more detailed walk through, for those of you with administrative rights: Step 1: Create the New Role Go to Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles . Click Add a new role . Use Choose a role to duplicate and select Non-editing teacher . Name the role (e.g., "Grader View") and provide a short description. Scroll down to the capability moodle/grade:viewhidden . Set this capability to Prevent to ensure this role cannot view hidden grades. Click Create this role at the bottom of the page. Step 2: Allow Role Switching Stay in Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles . Click on the Edit icon next to the Teacher role. Find the section Allow role switches . Add the "Grader View" role to the list of roles that teachers can switch to. Save changes. Step 3: Switch to the Grader View Role The teacher logs into Moodle and enters the course. They can switch roles by accessing the user menu (often top right) and selecting Switch role to... > Grader View . The Grader Report in this role will exclude hidden items, showing only the grades that students can see. Step 4: Return to Normal Role To switch back to the normal teaching role, the teacher should select Return to my normal role from the user menu. Hope this helps!

Moodle's grade book doesn't use the word "null" because most students don't know database language. A dash is better. This is because many assignments are not available to the student, yet. It's the "attempt" of a quiz that changes the "rawgrade" from null to a value, not the grade book. If a student doesn't attempt the quiz, "rawgrade" remains "null." You have thrown in "overall grades." Overall Grades are not in this grades_grades table. Exclude empty grade, as far as I know, also is not contained in the grades_grades table. You have also thrown in one more concept, "partially attempted." What do you mean? Did the student start a quiz, but not "submit?" If so, this is still a null in grades_grades. Did the student begin a quiz, not finish, yet submit? If so, Moodle will see this as completed. But the student might not. This is why you must explain to students what they must or should not do when taking a quiz. Multiple tables are "related" to produce what you see in the student's grade book.  If you want just the student's final course grade, I believe it is in a different table. Returning to your initial question, the student grade book is designed not to show "null" but instead a dash (-) for null grades. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook setups
ResponsesInList.Text: "What I cannot figure out is, if a student did not attempt or even login into the course, how to get the null entries created in the grade_grades? I want to see all NULL values for that course not attempted." I believe that Moodle creates the items in grade_grades (administratively) when a student is added to a course based on all activities that are TO BE graded. They are like empty buckets, just waiting for the student to complete them. They show NULL because students have not submitted them. I don't think they have anything to do with the student logging into a course. Moodle keeps track of courses students have logged into in different tables, such as logstore_standard_log. And there are other tables that keep track of whether or not a student has entered a quiz, and other states of activity. Remember, Moodle uses a relational database model. Moodle 4.4 has around 500 tables, as I recall.  I see around 13 tables that begin with "mdl_quiz_" and around 27 that begin with "mdl_question."  There's a graphic model (somewhere) that will show which tables are connected to grades_grades.  Then, there is also logic about how tables are propagated with rows.  It's not simple! Below is the SQL query I used in Moodle 3.11 to produce students' final course grades. I can't guarantee it will work for you, but I am sharing it as an example. I used 8 tables in it.  If you are good with SQL, it might make some sense to you.  I haven't explored this code for Moodle 4 yet. CREATE VIEW rjfinalgrades AS SELECT c.shortname AS CourseShortname, u.lastname AS LastName, u.firstname AS FirstName, u.email AS Email, gg.finalgrade as FinalGrade, c.idnumber AS CourseIDNum, c.id AS CourseNumber, ue.userid AS StudentNumber, 3 AS MoodleVersion FROM mdl_course c JOIN mdl_enrol e ON e.courseid = c.id JOIN mdl_user_enrolments ue ON ue.enrolid = e.id JOIN mdl_context con ON con.instanceid = c.id JOIN mdl_role_assignments ra ON (ra.contextid = con.id AND ra.userid = ue.userid) JOIN mdl_user u ON u.id = ue.userid JOIN mdl_grade_items gi ON gi.courseid = c.id JOIN mdl_grade_grades gg ON (gg.itemid = gi.id AND gg.userid = ue.userid) WHERE e.status = 0 AND ue.status = 0 AND ra.roleid = 5 AND c.idnumber > 200 AND u.idnumber < 99995 AND gi.itemtype = "course" AND ue.userid > 0 ORDER BY c.idnumber DESC, u.lastname, u.firstname

ResponsesInList.Title: Reduce size of bar/row in v4.3 Grader Report?
ResponsesInList.Text: Just an FYI that this footer also serves as the pagination if you have more then 50 users enrolled (depending on the default # of users to display in the gradebook set at the site-admin level). The CSS is tricky in my theme because I was able to get the padding to 0, but there was still a minimum height for the sticky footer -- and after reducing that hight, it caused the position of the Overall Averages (if enabled) to also then need to be adjusted... (and then needs to also be ajusted in mobile mode), but feel free to play around based on your theme classes: #page-grade-report-grader-index .stickyfooter {height: auto;} #page-grade-report-grader-index .sticky-footer-content.px-3.py-2 {padding: .25rem !important;} For the activity headers... I believe the hight you're seeing is due to making room for the longest titled activity in your gradebook. you could consider adding some CSS to clip text longer than 3 lines, for example. Again, would need to be modified for your theme, but this worked for me: .path-grade-report-grader .heading .gradeitemheader { white-space: normal; text-overflow: ellipsis; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 3; -webkit-box-orient: vertical;}

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing CSV line breaks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing CSV line breaks
ResponsesInList.Text: You can split your comments into as many lines as you want, as long as the whole comment string for each username is wrapped around one set of quotes. And comments can be of variable lengths on multiple lines for each username: username,gradeitem_name,grade,comments A12345,Quiz ABC,80, " Multi-line comment for user A12345. With this showing on a new line. And three more lines below this. Approved by Heather Headmaster And checked by Charlie Checker. Using Formula ABZ246XYC "

ResponsesInList.Title: Students should be able to see Overall Feedback from Quizzes when they view their "Grades"
ResponsesInList.Text: Students should be able to see Overall Feedback from Quizzes when they view their "Grades" Pedagogical and andragogical research is unequivocal - feedback helps all students; grades alone only help some students in some ways Students can view Quiz feedback by visiting the quiz, but seeing all the feedback in one place makes it more impactful and holistically meaningful Instructors can input feedback manually, but this is time-consuming, and many instructors use a Quiz module because they have too many students to get feedback turned around in a timely manner One of the best uses of a Quiz with closed-ended items is to provide immediate feedback to students that  allows for them to self-correct their understanding; without feedback, this is harder The Assignment activity is able to pass feedback to the Gradebook, and does, meaning it should be relatively simple for the Quiz module to pass feedback as well There is an argument that the Gradebook should only show feedback an instructor has manually entered, however, the point of "Overall Feedback" on a Quiz is to provide a general encouragement or remediation suggestion based upon the students' overall earned grade - and the instructor decides what that statement should be, and what conditions trigger it, so any such feedback is, actually, still owned by the instructor Quizzes have many "feedback" options; the Overall Feedback is straightforward for any type of quiz and would be easiest to send to Gradebook plugin

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course final Calculations
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, you can put the assessments in a category, with the desired weightings, then for the course total use grade calculation https://docs.moodle.org/403/en/Grade_calculation give the asessment category and each of the grades an id, say A1, A2, Atotal for the category then =if(min( a1 , a2 )<65,0, Atotal ) so if the minimum of assessments is under 65, return 0, otherwise return the calcuation for the assessment grade with weightings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Do not count empty grades with formulas
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I need to know how to do this. I have several categories items with a grades and I need to calc the global grade using these items with a formula, calculating the average of these items. My problem is I want to see the real average in all moment, that is to say, if I have 3 items with grades, the average is with this 3 grades, and when I finish the next topic, the average must be of 4 items. And so on, as the coruse progresses, the average adds more items. This is an example; Category 1: Cat1 Quizz 1 Quizz 2 Exam 1 Grade Category 1 --> pond. average of quizz 1, quizz2 and exam. (Automatic calculate by gradebook) Category 2: Cat2 Quizz 1 Exam 2

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do not count empty grades with formulas
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there! Here is the cleaner way to do this, with no calculation! If I understand this right, you have Category 1 & 2, which have real grades, and Category 3, which you're using to average the two categories. You should put Category 1 and 2 into Category 3, and set Category 3 to "mean of grades" and exclude empty grades, instead of using a grade calculation. Here is the harder way to do this, with a calculation! If you're set on using grade calculations, try using "=if(x,y,z)". The function returns y if x is true (or not zero), and returns z if x is false (or zero). So, you could do it like this: =if( CAT2 ,average( CAT1 , CAT2 ), CAT1 ) This says that if CAT2 is zero, then it returns CAT1. If CAT2 is not zero, then it returns an average of CAT1 and CAT2. Using the calculation will probably result in issues down the line.  Using categories makes it much easier to understand if you spend some time away from gradebook setup. Hope this works!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do not count empty grades with formulas
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks you for your answer, but in my case, the gradebook is too complicated. There are 9 CAT and I need the average of this 9 CAT but it will be completed in June and I need to show the real average while the course is advancing. I use a similar expression. Thanks you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do not count empty grades with formulas
ResponsesInList.Text: Not too complicated! Make a CAT 10, put all of the other 9 categories into it, set it to weighted mean of grades, and exclude empty grades. This will average the totals of all 9 categories and exclude any empty scores so that you can show the real average while the course is advancing. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Brian. We had to remove the tab indices with a value greater than 0 in MDL-79057 as this has been raised in the accessibility audit for Moodle 4.2 and thus fails WCAG 2.1 Level AA Success Criterion (SC) 2.4.3: Focus Order . We need to avoid using a tab index greater than 0 as this can lead to an unexpected tab order that will make it difficult for people who rely on keyboard navigation to operate on the page. Below is a screenshot of the tab order for the Single view report from the accessibility audit report: As you can see, the tab order is quite all over the place which makes it difficult for keyboard-only users to navigate the page. For sighted users, it will be quite difficult to predict where the next focusable element will go after the last grade input without prior experience and knowledge of how the page works. I imagine this is worse for people with visual impairments, as it would be quite difficult and confusing where they are on the page if the focus moves in different parts of the grade table when they tab through it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Gradebook Assignment Weightings by Group
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello: I have two groups in my course that reflect different course sections : Group A and Group B. The syllabus has different assignment weightings according to each course section as follows: Group A Group B Assignment #1 30% 20% Assignment #2 70% 50% Assignment #3 -- 30% Both groups submit their respective assignments into the same "assignment" block. (i.e., when professor goes to grade Assignment #1, he/she will see both groups submitting and grade altogether). NB: Assignment #3 is hidden for Group A students, obviously. I want the gradebook to take grades given for each assignment and weigh them differently when showing students their overall grades in the gradebook. I cannot figure out how to do this. I think there might be a way with "grade categories" but I haven't figured it out/been able to test. Thoughts?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook Assignment Weightings by Group
ResponsesInList.Text: Gradebook questions are always difficult to address because the grade book is both very flexible and complex. I think you can do what you wish to do. Assignment #3 would only be available to Group B. In the grade book, the 100% would distribute itself for assignments #1 and #2 for Group A, and then among all three assignments for Group B. Some of this will depend upon your weighting scheme. You should study the grade book docs, and then mock this up in a dummy course with dummy students. It might take you some practice to assure that everything is working correctly. When you get into this, give yourself some time and make sure to relax. You will probably not be able to knock this out in 10 minutes. It might take several hours.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook Assignment Weightings by Group
ResponsesInList.Text: We did something similar in a course. In course management -> Edit course settings we set Groups to Separate). In the gradebook we created separate categories and excluded empty grades for that category. Then in the assignment settings restricted access (with closed eye) to the specific group; added the assignment as necessary to the the appropriate category. For a short example Cat A @ 20% Assignment 1 (group A) = 70% Assignment 1 (group b) = 50% Assignment 2 (group A - 30% ..... The category seemed to total all assignments together, so that's why we used exclude empty grades. As group A would not do Group B assignments and there fore would have an empty grade for those. The restrict access (with closed eye) helps clean up the student view of the gradebook as they wouldn't see the other groups assignments in their gradebook. The "exclude" feature could also work, but that might require review every time the course is offered.

ResponsesInList.Title: Add Additional Column in Single  View
ResponsesInList.Text: We often have a few students with identical name in same course. It is very challenging to make sure grades are assigned correctly in current Gradebook-Single view layout. Is there any way to add an additional column such as username or student number in Gradebook-Single view?

ResponsesInList.Title: Add Additional Column in Single  View
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - so the Single View doesn't show the columns selected in User Policies to display alongside where ever a user's name is displayed, however, you can utilize the Alternate Name field in users' profile. If you go to the users with identical names, edit their profiles, toggle "Additional Names" and fill in something for the Alternate Name field (such as a middle initial or anything unique that will help distinguish the two apart. Then, in Site Admin - Users - User Policies, change the Alternative Full Name format from "language" to something like "firstname (alternatename) lastname" (and the parentheses are optional, but I like them to help distinguish this Altname field between last names that have two words). Then, whereever this user is displayed, you'll see those that Alt name directly in their full name versus in a separate column. You can also control "who" can see that alt name by enabling the "viewfullnames" permission for specific roles. Note -- if the student has the ability to edit their profile, then they will see that field, can edit that field (though it is possible to lock that field down in the Site Admin - Plugins - Authentication - Manual accounts page)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'User' and 'Myself' see different percentages in "Contribution to course total'
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem arose through the default settings which do not include hidden assessments in the weightings towards the course total. Hidden assessments are hidden from the students but also hidden from Gradebook. This means that the contribution to course total was skewed. The screenshot below shows the correct contribution. (There is another assessment coming with a 40% weighting.) In the original post, because only one assessment was visible, the contribution towards the course total was also shown as 60%, which was obviously false as the assessment contribution was only 60% of 30% of the course total (18%). To fix the problem we went to 'Course grade settings': Scroll down to 'Overview report' and select 'Show totals including hidden items': Then scroll to the bottom of the page to 'Hide totals if they contain hidden items' and select 'Show  totals if they contain hidden items' Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Course Completion using course grade total based on passing grades versus activity completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 3.9 The workplace courses in my environment often change with new grading activities often added  or swapped (i.e. a  Quiz gets replaced by a graded SCORM activity). Any suggestions welcome.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading using Rubrics + manual grade
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, this might be a terrible suggestion but it's the first thing that comes to mind that I would do so I'll share -- determine the max score of your rubric as-is (ie let's say it's 20), then add one more criterion row that has 80 items in it (making the rubric out of 100 now) so you could use that row to add as many point into the existing rubric score to make the final grade your desired score that you would have otherwise done manually. Then everyone gets their feedback and a final score that you have almost/partially manually calculated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Penalty Applied to Final Grade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Penalty Applied to Final Grade
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, should be doable. First, how do you plan to keep track of attendance? Do you plan to make Attendance its own grade book category, counted but worth no grade book points? It's up to you. You could always put attendance into a hidden grade category, which could show in the grade book. In some courses I have taught where I want to use attendance, I simply put attendance into its own grade category and make it contribute to the final grade, like 5%. This way, you don't need to "adjust" the final grade because it is already built into the calculation. However, the Moodle grade book allows "equations," as shown below. The Moodle docs do a good job explaining this, but I warn you that it is a little complex. If you decide to use an equation, set up a dummy course and dummy students and practice. As I recall, there is an Attendance plugin for Moodle. I have never used it. As another idea, you can create grade items that you manually update, if you are coordinating attendance that you keep in another system, or on paper. Moodle can "import" grades (I recall a CSV file). Many years ago, when I taught in a physical classroom, I enjoyed using "clickers" for in-class quizzing. I was then able to use this clicker data also to keep track of attendance. No clicks; the student was absent!

ResponsesInList.Title: A plea for review - Gradebook and only 'Natural'
ResponsesInList.Text: Basically : The gradebook was showing what appeared to be inaccurate results.  This is a course originally developed in Moodle3 and now in M4.0.4.  The aggregation method for all categories and course total is "Simple weighted mean of grades." Here is a specific student's s ample category totals and overall grade: 90% - Cat 1 93% - Cat 2 100% - Cat 3 Overall: 89% The main issue : I had an assignment (that I wanted marked but not counted in their overall grade) where the student scored 80% that was not in a specific category but Moodle was still counting it anyway in the Overall mark .  I tried setting this assignment as 'Extra Credit' and then the Overall mark became 100% (not at all what I was after).  So then I tried to make a category that would be hidden and not counted where I could place this assignment but I couldn't change this new category's Overall Category mark (greyed out).  And then, after some research, I learned that in Moodle4, only the 'Natural' aggregation method is available by default....  So, I turned on ' Simple weighted mean of grades', set the category total to 0, hid it, and presto.  Good to go. Obviously, Moodle is trying to restrict course's aggregation methods but I'm unsure as to why.  Certainly in my circumstance, it made things far more challenging (and added a few more greys and wrinkles than I would have liked).  Could we consider returning these aggregation methods or perhaps providing some notification informing the teacher as to why they can't adjust the category value?

(Example: Category one has a weight of 50, category two has a weight of 30, and category three has a weight of 20. The student has a 100% in the first two categories, but the final category is for the Final Exam, so it doesn't have a grade in it yet, but I want the course total to 100% not 80%) I have attempted to achieve this in many ways, but have run into issues, I tried "natural" grading aggregation for the course (with "mean of grades with extra credit" for the category grading aggregation), which is what I think it should be, and it works for the categories, but then it doesn't properly account for the empty grade categories when figuring out the course total. It is the example in number 4 that is giving the course total of 80%. In courses without empty categories it works fine. I have tried a bunch of the "mean of grades" "mean of grades with extra credit" "Weighted Mean of Grades" for the course grading aggregation while using "mean of grades with extra credit" and "mean of grades" for the category grade aggregation but for some reason on three of my courses it doesn't calculate the course total correctly. The total percentage is a few percent off. On one class the category total is also off. In that specific class both the category and the course have a higher percentage then the max that is allow. (Example: 100.5 out of 100.) The category is also more than is allowed, and it is set to "mean of grades" grading aggregation. The other two the course total is off by a few percent. Up or down, for some reason. In every situation I have the "exclude empty grades" box checked. So my questions are: What grade aggregation should I be using? Why, well the use case might look like this: As a course creator I need to follow a predefined grading system as set out in curriculum documents.  I am not an expert on grade calculations. I would like a tool I can use help me with grade calculations so that I can be sure I have my grade book set up correctly. As a Moodle Administrator I am somewhat of a grade calculation expert, or can at least confidently follow the docs. I would like consistency in the courses so I can be assured of the robustness of learner results. As a learner I want my grades to add up correctly so that I can continue to focus on the areas of learning I need to focus on. Before I release this on the Moodle plugins , I'd appreciate some further testing and feedback on the usefulness of such a tool. If you are interested you can download the plugin from https://github.com/noisyjerm/moodle-gradereport_calcsetup/archive/refs/heads/master.zip Install it onto a development site, not a production site as it is not ready for that yet. Install it into the /grades/report/ directory There is an example course included which will be helpful in seeing how it works. If you have any comments or suggestions please reply here. Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook If-statement text output?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, The gradebook calculations won't accept a string like that. However, you can accomplish the same thing in a different way. If you change the lab category grade type from "Value" to "Scale", you can make a custom scale that consists of "Labs missing", "Labs passed". The two text values of the scale correspond to numeric values 0 and 1, so you can replace your above formula with: =If(LAB1+LAB2+LAB3+LAB4+LAB5>=4, 1, 0)

ResponsesInList.Title: Showing students both "grade so far" and "total grade"
ResponsesInList.Text: When we configure gradebooks, we have the option of showing students the "grade so far in the class" but not factoring in ungraded items in the gradebook. E.g. Assume there are 10 assignments, but only one has already passed the due date Assume if a student got 80% on that first item, but still have zeros for the other 9 items. In one view of the grades, The student would see "80%" -- how well they've done so far in the class. Another view would be "8%" -- they have received e.g. (10 * 0.80) / (10 * 10) of the possible points in the class. In Canvas, you can only configure the gradebook to show option #1 and students complain when that grade decreases (they think it should only increase). In Moodle, you can configure the gradebook to show either view, but you can't easily let the student see view #1 AND view #2 -- there's a change you have to make & communicate to the students. Is there a better solution to this problem? Having a toggle button that shows views as #1 or #2 for a specific student would be useful (or just always show both views in some way).

ResponsesInList.Title: Showing students both "grade so far" and "total grade"
ResponsesInList.Text: What my staff does to help with this is the following: instead of students starting the year with an "F" and watching the numerator slowly rise, they instead see the denominator slowly rise one week at a time. To accomplish this, we have all of our gradebook category aggregations set to "Natural" and we have 4 sub-categories within the main Course Toal category -- one for each quarter. Inside each quarter category, we have 10 additional sub-categories, one for each week. At the start of the year, we check the box for "Excludes work not yet submitted" in every single gradebook category's settings. This way, the gradebook is only counting work the student has submitted instead of counting everything. Then, on Monday mornings, the teachers edit the gradebook category for the week that just passed and they "uncheck" that "Excludes work not yet submitted" setting. This way, the gradebook now counts the previous week against the student (plus any work submitted outside that week). As each week passes, the gradebook denominator slowly builds. At the start of the final week of the quarter, week 10, teachers "uncheck" that "Excludes..." setting for the "previous" week's category, the "current" week's category, and the "current Quarter" parent-category. This way, for the entire last week of the quarter, students see that 'all work' for the weeks 1 - 10 of that quarter now counts and the gradebook gives an accurate picture of the the final quarter grade if they were to 'stop' working that week. Despite the weekly "prep work" for my staff, this has worked well for our students so I wanted to share.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Pass/Fail Giving More Credit to Fail
ResponsesInList.Text: There are a few older posts about the lack of functionality on the scales. No you can't change a scale after they have a relationship with a student. I created many bad, useless scales. I found that it is easier to use the grade>letters values that to use scales. This is only more forgiving. Edit the grade letters from the A-F scales to whatever values you desired for Pass and Fail. Remove the other values that will not be used.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Pass/Fail Giving More Credit to Fail
ResponsesInList.Text: Don't even attempt fixing this, it will be a mess. When creating a scale it clearly says you need to work from low to high, not the other way around. Keep the values 'as is', because changing the values will result in every student failing when they passed before and the other way around. Start next year with the correct scales. Wait 10 years and the problem is usually gone

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course grade and certificate
ResponsesInList.Text: Here are a couple ideas (not guaranteed to be any good 😀): Set up a separate assignment, or the course total grade to have a custom grade calculation: https://docs.moodle.org/311/en/Grade_calculations Use "Restriction sets", and exhaustively add all possible combinations (10, when choosing 3 from 5) as separate restrictions. Then, set the overall restriction conditions so it is "Student must match any of the following". With some nifty nested restrictions, maybe it could be done in less?

ResponsesInList.Title: Nested 'If' statements or alternative gradebook calculations
ResponsesInList.Text: Running Moodle 3.8+ I have a scenario where there are five quizzes in a course, and all have a pass mark of 75. The users are allowed to 'fail' one of those, but as long as they get at least 60 in that failure they will be considered as ok to move forwards. If they get less than 60 in one or more then they fail the entire course. Quizzes are in categories - one per quiz - and the quizzes are tagged as '001', '002', etc. The grade calculation per category are currently like this (note the double brackets moodle calculations requires converts the text in here, so I've left them out around the item ID numbers): =if(001>=60,001+0,0) If the student scores below 60 then the category records that as zero... we currently total up the categories in the usual manner. What I am looking for is a way to evaluate whether more than one quiz is showing less than 60 out of the five, and if so to record the entire course as a fail. If one is below 75 then check if it is below 60. If it is, fail the course, if not, pass the course and issue a certificate. Something like this: IF(COUNTIF(001,002,003,004,005,">=60")>3,SUM(001+002+003+004+005),0) I can do this in a spreadhseet using 'countif' and 'if' statements, but I think the way I am doing it is a little too intense for Moodle; it appears to reject countif in this format.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Nested 'If' statements or alternative gradebook calculations
ResponsesInList.Text: I have had a response to this here ... the answer was to use grade categories and add a few manual grade items, with custom calculations. Whilst it is a little complex in the math, it's also quite straightforward once you get your head around the equations! Thanks due to Dominique for his really very good response.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students can't see activities they have not attempted
ResponsesInList.Text: Do you have any restrict access rules on your activities or sections that contain the activities that are not displaying? Here is what I think goes on in the gradebook when it comes to restrict access rules: • If an activity is "available" on the course page to a student, then they see it as a clickable link in the gradebook. • If the activity has visible restrictions (eye ball not slashed) and is "not yet available" to the student, then they see it as un-clickable text in the gradebook. • If the Topic/Section containing the activity is restricted to the student, and the activity itself has no restrictions or no visible restrictions (eyeball slashed), then they do not see it in the gradebook. • If the Topic/Section containing the activity is restricted to the student, and the activity itself has visible restrictions (eyeball not slashed), then they see it in the gradebook as un-clickable text.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I need a graph/formula for grade offset and multiplicator
ResponsesInList.Text: Happy to help if I can, but I'm not entirely sure what you're trying to do. As I understand it, you want to covert a 0-24 rubric to a 10 point maximum in the gradebook, with the rubric's 16 translating to 5.5? If so, I am surprised you're saying that multiplicator=1.35 and offset=-3.5 works. By my math, they shouldn't (24 * 1.35 - 3.5 = 28.9; and 16 * 1.35 - 3.5 = 18.1). A rubric score of 0, for example, will be -3.5 in the gradebook. Is this the effect you're looking for?

ResponsesInList.Title: Make Gradebook Category become Excluded when all Activities within are Excluded
ResponsesInList.Text: I've made MDL-71197 regarding a suggestion to make Gradebook Categories become Excluded when all activities within are excluded and wanted to post here for discussion. Summary: When one goes into the gradebook Single View and clicks "Exclude" next to an activity, it drops the points earned/available for that activity from the category total in which those activities are contained (as well as from categories at higher context ). Teachers love this feature – it makes it so easy to differentiate for various student needs so students aren't held accountable for all activities. The problem is, if a teacher Excludes "ALL" activities in a given gradebook category, the points earned/available do NOT become excluded UNLESS the teacher also Excludes the gradebook category that contains these activities. ResponsesInList.Title: How are grades calculated?

So for example, I have a few categories that have several assignments in them (like labs and exams).  I want my Labs to be worth 25% of the overall grade and exams to be worth 35%.  As long as each lab is worth the same amount (say 100 pts) then the points calculation method will be the same as using an average method? My dilemma is this... Each lab assignment may have different labs for them.  Chapter 1 might have 3 labs to complete and chapter 2 might have 6.  I still want them to carry the same weight, Chapter 1 labs is worth the same towards the Labs average as Chapter 2 labs.  The only way I see to do this is to set the points for Chapter 1 labs and Chapter 2 labs to the same value (say 100 pts).  Is this correct?  I cannot set the Chapter 1 points to 300 and Chapter 2 points to 600 otherwise the chapter 2 labs have more effect on the overall grade, right? The way I have always graded is to set the number of points an assignment is worth to whatever I want (max score).  Then to calculate the lab average, my formula converts each individual assignment to a % adds them up and divides by the number of labs.  In this method, each lab is worth the same amount.  The gradebook in Moodle does not appear to work this way by default.  Is there a way to change this behavior? OR am I forced to make each lab worth the same # of points (say 100) and covert the grades manually? Thanks is advance, MK

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How are grades calculated?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am a little confused as to what exactly you are trying to achieve here...you say you want them the same weight but then you talk about having to manually change grades if you set them to the same weight... In the gradebook, you can set weights separately to the grade if you have it set to natural grading. Just check the box and change the weight amount. Or set the points for each lab to total to 100. If you have two labs, make them 50 points each, three labs 33.33 each, etc...or you could put each assignment in its own category and then set it however you want...there are multiple ways to set the gradebook up - I am pretty sure one will let you achieve what you want.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How are grades calculated?
ResponsesInList.Text: If i'm understanding what you want, it's to have different points for labs but each still contribute the same % to the course total percentage, I think you'll need to assign a weight to the category (25% for labs) and then assign weights to each lab (E.g. 10% per lab if there are 10 labs) within that category.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [3.9]Minimum grade for assignment

I recall that thread! Still wish there was flexibility on this. Since then, I've just ended up doing this with gradebook category calculations. If your interested, give the assignment an ID and then, in the gradebook setup, wrap the assignment in a category that has

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to make an activity *not count* toward the course total in the Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Audrey, Here's how I make an activity not count towards the course total in the gradebook: Go Gradebook setup. Find the activity you don't want to count, then in the weights column, tick the box and change the weight to zero. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Save changes button. The grades will then be recalculated. If you like, you can try things out on our School demo site , where any changes you make are wiped clean when the site resets on the hour.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove "Whole Forum" from gradebook item
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Pat, One solution would be to use the Language customisation feature. After choosing the language you wish to customise, such as English, select forum.php as component, enter the string identifier gradeitemnameforwholeforum and change the text from 
```text
Whole forum grade for {$a->name}
```
 to 
```text
{$a->name}
```
 then save changes to the language pack.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove "Whole Forum" from gradebook item

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove "Whole Forum" from gradebook item [Solved]
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi again Pat, You're not the only person wanting to remove "Whole forum" from the gradebook item, as the problem has been reported as MDL-70379 ! As I mentioned in a comment in the issue, please note that any language string changes will only take effect when you create a new forum. For an existing forum, you need to go to the forum settings page and save changes. Also, for anyone browsing this discussion, please note that the English language strings gradeitemnameforrating and gradeitemnameforwholeforum are going to be improved so that the name of the forum comes before the words 'whole forum grade' e.g. Neutrino Discussion whole forum grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading is very slow when using overrides
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all got a very strange issue with the gradebook. A course has 141 gradable items in the gradebook and there are 500 users enrolled in the course in approx 33 groups. The issue arises when grading a only a few of the users at a time manually. We graded 38 users who where in a group in the course using the bulk method but this took over 500 seconds to complete. If we however bulk graded all of the users in the course this takes only a few seconds. This would indicate it takes much longer when grading a few number of users than it does if grading all of them using the bulk method. Which you would think is counter intuitive. After many hours of research i think the issue is with moodle/browse/grade/report/singleview/classes/local/ui/override.php The function called  public function set($value) is as follows: public function set($value) { if (empty($this->grade->id)) { return false; } $state = $value == 0 ? false : true; $this->grade->set_overridden($state); $this->grade->grade_item->force_regrading(); return false; } From the above it looks like each time this is called for every item in the gradebook for each of the 38 users (38 times 141) it forces a regrade of the gradebook before it goes to the next item which needs to be dealt with. Instead it should only run the regrade once all the entries in the grade book has been updated then run the regrade not after each item is changed. Does this make sense as i think this is a bug or at least an improvement which needs to be changed.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to use Natural aggregation as mean of grades in moodle 3.8 or 3.9
ResponsesInList.Text: With "Natural" aggregation, the category will always be a sum of the activities within (so the total will always be 300 in your first example). What the statement in the Docs refers to is that instead of each 100 pt assignment having a 33% weight, you can change the weights of the three activities so the weights are different, yet still sum to 300. This is to help you make quick weighting changes without having to go into every activity and change the total point value.

ResponsesInList.Text: I figure after an hour of searching the forums it is safe to post. I set up a scale: Incomplete/Complete and I'm using it in a Weighted category in a Weighted Mean of Grades gradebook. What the heck is the (2) showing under this scale? Two items - the fact that I am using two words in this scale? It's not the total possible, right? Because that should be a "1" if I'm understanding scales properly. Incomplete,Complete = 0,1. I've attached a screenshot from my demo course. Thanks in advance, Bobby

ResponsesInList.Title: What is (number) under scale in Gradebook Setup?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, yes it's because you're using two items in your scale. 0 (no rating), 1 (your first item, incomplete), and 2. (Your second item, complete). The assignments are already incomplete in their Non-submitted state, so you don't need it in your scale - if the submission is incomplete, you can leave feedback without assigns a grade. You could also have "partially complete" as your first scale item. Otherwise, you'll just want 1 one term scale - "complete" to gain a 0,1 scenario.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Extra credit complex calculations (3.7)
ResponsesInList.Text: I also use "extra credit" in my courses, so I am a little familiar with what you might be trying to do. First, however, you say "So, they can get an extra 10 points if they do 10 or more of these quizzes." What do you mean? Must they do at least 10 before they get any points, or are you allowing something like 1 point per attempt, up to a maximum of 10 points? Also, is their score on these attempt irrelevant? Be careful, if their score is not relevant, then you might create an incentive to just click away, blindly. In my courses, I put "bonus" exercises into their own grade book category. These accumulate, and the student can add 2% to their final grade if they have all bonus points. So what happens is that students can score a 100% in the course if they do perfectly on all regular assignments, or they can score 100% for the course if they score 98% on all regular assignments, plus the 2% extra credit. Moodle's grade book provides for extra credit, and it supports exactly what I want to do. (Oh, I also have a bonus-bonus grade item, but this gets a little complex.) So, getting back to your question, yes, one might be able to create equations to do what they want. However, I put all extra-credit into a grade book category and make that category be extra-credit. Whatever you decide to do, make sure to practice. Moodle's grade book is extremely powerful, but there are also many subtle features. Be mentally prepared and give yourself time, otherwise you will go crazy. Also, read the docs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Harmony, The gradebook and course grade aggregation is a bit of a challenge, I can understand that. What I think is happening, is the following: In your site, under Site administration > Grades > Grade category settings, check if the default aggregation of grades is set to 'Natural'. This setting determines how a course grade is calculated by default. The 'Natural' aggregation is basically a sum of all grades a participant can get in the course. In your case, that's 8 * 100 points = 800. If you wish to set this to another grade aggregation, this is also the page to select a more useful one, such as Mean of grades. You can then check if you can change the grade aggregation method in your course through Grades > Gradebook setup, by clicking Edit > Edit settings for the topmost grade category (which will correspond with your course's name). Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Non-linear grade calculations in Moodle gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi all, I don't know if this one has been asked before, but here it goes: In Dutch educational institutions, we see a common practice to calculate grades in a somewhat non-linear fashion, like in this chart: The idea is, that a passing percentage of 70 equals a 5.5 grade out of 10. Any score over or equal to 70% follows formula 1: 
```text
=(((
item1
-70)*(4.5/(100-70)))+5.5)
```
 And anything below 70% follows formula 2: 
```text
=(((
item1
)*(4.5/70))+1)
```
 Would it be possible to combine these two formulas in one manual grade item calculation? And if so, how? And if this isn't possible, how do I assure the student participant sees the correct grade I calculated?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Non-linear grade calculations in Moodle gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Sometimes, it pays to investigate and play to find a solution. The Moodle Docs aren't really clear on how to create this kind of non-linear formulas for grade items, but I found the following: the proper 'if' formula is constructed this way: 
```text
=if(condition, (calculation), else)
```
 For a Quiz that has a maximum of 100 points, with idnumber 'item1' and the conditions that I elaborated above, this becomes: 
```text
=if(
item1
>=70;(((
item1
-70)*(4,5/(100-70)))+5,5);(((
item1
)*(4,5/70))+1))
```
 You can replace the tipping value of 70 with whichever value you'd need. ';' and ',' are there because of Dutch langpack, these would need to be replaced with ',' and '.' for English.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can teacher add personal (private) notes or comments to grade book?
ResponsesInList.Text: One option would be to go to "Gradebook Setup" in the Administration block. Scroll to the bottom fo the Setup page, and click "Add Grade Item" -- give the grade item a name, such as "Teacher Notes" and set the maximum grade to "0" and save. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding grade from users
ResponsesInList.Text: If you consider my method below, I recommend creating a test course and test all the settings from a student and teacher role before making any changes. You could set up a multiple activity course that you are using to collect basic quiz results, and then use Assignment to collect another set of evaluation data. Gradebook Setup - create a category with both activities - and your passing score value that is the Course Total. Hide the entire Category - For the Category settings, the checkbox Exclude empty grades must be selected. Only display the Course Total to the student. Course requires restrictions - Hide Assignment until Quiz receives a passing grade. In the Quiz settings, review responses conditions, deselect the Marks checkbox. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using the percentage total of a "natural" grade category
ResponsesInList.Text: I made this happen in a test course. Here's how to do it: Set up gradebook like this, where you have two categories inside a "Non-Adjusted Course Total" category. I have put some grade items in there for testing & demonstration: Then open grade calculations for the course total at the bottom of the page: Set the ID numbers in the grade calcucations page to "CAT1" for the first Category, "CAT2" for the Second Category, and "NA_COURSETOTAL" for the third category. Now input the following formula in the grade calculation: =if(AND( NA_COURSETOTAL >=300, CAT1 >=200, CAT2 >=100), NA_COURSETOTAL ,min(299, NA_COURSETOTAL )) NOTE - those blue texts above are meant to have double brackets around them - see picture - they are displaying here as hyperlinks I think (thanks markdown). Replace the "300" with the 50% value of CAT1, Replace "100" with the 50% value of CAT2, and replace "299" with one integer below the 50% value of the whole course. This will freeze the student's grade at just under 50% until both categories have reached 50%. Here is how this is calculating in my demo course: Hope that helps - Happy Moodling!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using the percentage total of a "natural" grade category
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thank you, Ryan, for you effort to set up your example! I have now found an even better way to implement my gradebook: Here I switched to "Simple weighted mean" to get to percentages of the categories, which then are combined into the weighted mean. Additionally, to get the 50% constraint on each category, I introduced the additional grade item "Minimum Of Categories", defined as 
```text
=min(
C1
,
C2
)
```
 . This is then combined with the weighted mean via "Lowest grade" to get the overall grade. It this way, the use of custom calculation formulas is minimized. My only concern is: I have found the Moodle issue Enable change of maximum grade for grade aggregation method "Natural" , saying that "Simple Weighted Mean" might at some point be replaced by "Natural". Is that true? Then I would need that issue to be fixed, s.t. "Natural" can replace SWM in my course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using the percentage total of a "natural" grade category
ResponsesInList.Text: Clever! Any time you can minimize calculations is better, but I wonder if the user will be given the lowest grade of the two categories in every case instead of the average of the two categories once 50% is reached in both. I may have misunderstood the problem or the solution above. Either way if it works do it! I'm not on the gradebook development team so I am not certain about this, but I think Natural is meant to be the one aggregation that rules them all. In your case (a category where there is a 5 point assignment and a 6 point assignment that add up to 100), the user would have to set the grade point values to a number (say 50) then weight the assignments to match the 5 and 6 point distribution (weights 45 and 55 respectively). You could also make those point values for the assignment 45 and 55 if you wish. Then, if you wanted to grade out of 5 then you would use a rubric in the assignment with a max 5 grade and it would scale up to whatever number the grade is. So, in that way natural could still achieve the aggregation you mention above. However, I don't think any of the aggregation methods are going away for some time. There are a lot of users out there that have these as parts of large enrollment online courses where messing with the grades would have a disastrous cascading effect. Again, if it's working I always say use it. If core does away with SWM in some future update, you can cross that bridge when we come to it.

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Ryan, you wrote "Clever! Any time you can minimize calculations is better, but I
wonder if the user will be given the lowest grade of the two categories
in every case instead of the average of the two categories once 50% is
reached in both. I may have misunderstood the problem or the solution
above. Either way if it works do it!" You are right, thanks for pointing out my mistake! I need to introduce a custom formula for my course total: 
```text
=IF(
CATMIN
<50, 
CATMIN
, 
WEIGHTED
)
```
 There, CATMIN is the computed minimum of categories, and WEIGHTED is the weighted mean.

ResponsesInList.Title: Grade Calculation: Replace lowest exam score with final exam score if the final exam is higher than the lowest exam
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, This is a solution for the following scenario. I thought it worth sharing: The teacher wants to replace the lowest exam score for a semester with the final exam score if the final exam is higher than the lowest exam score. The idea is that students who improve on the content in the final exam can recover some credit for an earlier exam by performing well on this final. Here is how to accomplish this in Moodle 3.7: Create the grade items, either as manual grade items, assignments, quizzes, or any other graded activity. We will call them Exam 1, Exam 2, Exam 3, and Final Exam. Put exams 1, 2, and 3 in their own categories. Edit the calculation for these three categories. Make sure you remember to put in the IDs for the grade items in this step. In the calculations below the IDs are EXAM1, EXAM2, EXAM3, and FINALEXAM. For the Category containing Exam 1, put this in the grade calculation box: =if(AND( EXAM1 <=min( EXAM1 , EXAM2 , EXAM3 ), FINALEXAM > EXAM1 ), FINALEXAM , EXAM1 ) For the Category containing Exam 2, put this in the grade calculation box: =if(AND( EXAM2 <=min( EXAM1 , EXAM2 , EXAM3 ), EXAM2 < EXAM1 , FINALEXAM > EXAM2 ), FINALEXAM , EXAM2 ) For the Category containing Exam 3, put this in the grade calculation box: =if(AND( EXAM3 <=min( EXAM1 , EXAM2 , EXAM3 ), EXAM3 < EXAM1 , EXAM3 < EXAM2 , FINALEXAM > EXAM3 ), FINALEXAM , EXAM3 ) The gradebook setup page looks like this. Everything here is contained in a category called "Exam Tests": Open the editing for the category calculations is here:

ResponsesInList.Title: [3.7] Editing first attempt not synchronized with gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Why is it so that when you edit the first attempt for an assignment, this is not reflected in the gradebook? To check this, do the following: Set up an assignment with 2 attempts, grade to pass 5.5, new attempts automatically until pass Grade first attempt with 4. This will reopen a second attempt The grade 4 will be pushed to the grade book Teacher made a mistake, edits the grade for attempt 1 into 5 The grade 5 will never be pushed to the grade book. Student now sees two grades for the assignment: the grade 5 on the assignment page, the grade 4 in the grade book. This leads to many questions. The current grade in the grade book should reflect the grade for the first attempt (5)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [3.7] Editing first attempt not synchronized with gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you sure that the teacher is not putting the grade from the first attempt right into the gradebook? What Moodle version? Have you verified this yourself?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [3.7] Editing first attempt not synchronized with gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, I have verified this myself in several Moodles. Please try it yourself Version number is (as mentioned) 3.7, but this has been carrying on for a long time. I'm pretty sure this is what happens in the background: Attempt one -> number is pushed to grade book New attempt is opened -> grade -1 is written to assign_grades for attempt 2. This of course is not copied to the grade book (a grade of minus 1 would be strange) From now on, the grade book only looks at the grade for the last attempt for this assignment. Which is attempt 2. But that currently has grade -1 so nothing happens to the grade book. The grade book is never monitoring what is entered in attempt 1 for the assignment, as it is irrelevant for the grade book: that should only store the grade with the highest attempt number To me this looks like a bug... but it might be design, I don't know. It could be fixed pretty easy if the grade book will always store the grade from the highest attempt except when the grade is minus 1, then the grade book should store the grade from the attempt before that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [3.7] Editing first attempt not synchronized with gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: See screenshot of student below: What happened here? Student has had 1 attempt. Teacher graded this 5.0 but made a mistake and changed this to 4.0. Student now see two grades: the grade from assign_grades attempt 1, which is 4.0 but also sees the old (wrong) grade 5.0 from (and in) the grade book. This grade has never been updated with the correct grade. In our institution the number of attempts for an assignment is pretty important. For example you get TWO attempts for every assignment. After turning in the first assignment, there can be a review with the student and the teacher. The first attempt can be corrected by the teacher based upon this review. So that is why grades for the first attempt sometimes are corrected... but of course the teacher can always make a mistake and should be able to correct the grade for the first attempt anyway. NB: there's NOT a higher attempt made than attempt one in this example. So the 5.0 you see above is not from attempt 2 or higher, it was the wrong grade entered at attempt ONE which has been corrected. Tabel assign_grades has stored the correct grade, however table grade_grades still shows the wrong grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Non-assessed items in Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: On the Moodle Documentation page for the gradebook there is some helpful information about creating a new Grade category and then moving the "non-graded" items to that Grade category. 1. At the Course Administration pane, select Gradebook setup 2. Add a category. At the Grade category section the Exclude empty grades checkbox must be deselected. 3. ResponsesInList.Title: Does calculating grade points in the range from MIN to MAX have to be so complicated? [M3.5]
ResponsesInList.Text: Please forgive my angry sub-tone if it should surface, as I have spent literally hours trying to configure Moodle 3.5 doing the very most basic task in managing grades, namely calculating a grade point between, say, 1 and 10 from the marks. I have a quiz with a total of 7 marks whose maximum grade I can set to 10 and this seems to set the maximum grade in the grade item settings to the same. The respective field is grayed out and I have not found any way to change its value. Probably that would not make much sense either. However, the minimum value should absolutely be editable but it also is locked down to the value 0 and I have not found any way of changing it either. In the site-wide general settings for grades there is a Boolean property "Show minimum grade" (grade_report_showmin, default = Yes) with the following short explanation: "Minimum grade is used in calculating grades and weights. If not shown, minimum grade will default to zero and cannot be edited." (<sarcasm>The explanation does not claim that the minimum grade can be edited when the minimum grade is shown.</sarcasm>) There does not seem to be any good way of solving this problem. The only propostion I found was defining a scale with 91 steps from 1.0 to 10.0 which, frankly speaking, as absurd an approach as a desperate one. Richard van Iwaarden raised the issue "[3.5]Minimum grade in gradebook can not be edited" here in this forum in January but has not received much feedback and the discussion thread died out end of February. Please look there for screen-shots. My work-around is to set the multiplicator to 0.9 and the offset to 1.0 . This way the boundary value 0 or 10 get mapped to 1 or 10, respectively, with linear interpolation in between. This seems way too much hassle for such a basic task. I must mention that after the frustrating hours of uselessly poking around in the settings, I was only glad that this finally worked. Two questions arise.: 1.) Does this have to be so complicated, or have I been overlooking anything obvious or otherwise well-known? 2.) Is the minimum value editable and effective in more recent versions of Moodle? PS: I just stumbled over the thread "Minimum and Maximum grades of a quiz can not be changed." raised by Visvanath Ratnaweera just a few weeks ago. For reasons that I cannot understand, there does not seem to be much hope to see this behavior changed. So I let my posting stand for the case that it can give other desperate Moodle users an idea for a work-around. Nevertheless, I would like to mention that several European countries use a grading system starting at 1 instead of 0. Germany uses an inverted scale from 6 (lowest grade) to 1 (highest grade). And I do not see any reason why a linear scaling from [0,maxMarks] to [minGrade,maxGrade] could not be easily implemented. Nevertheless I am thankful to all the developers for making Moodle available.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Set Gradebook to only display Course Total of Student's Grade Report
ResponsesInList.Text: Wow, that is a doozy! So it sounds like you set up your course once correctly, and then this bug popped up when you tried to copy it. I was able to reproduce it and added a comment to the tracker issue. From the development standpoint, I can kind of understand why it would behave this way. If you remove one or more grade items... how should the gradebook behave? How should it re-calculate all the relationships? How do you describe this exactly? Are there alternatives that make just as much sense? Would people be frustrated if it behaved one way and not the other? It's quite possible that there is a simple solution that I just cannot think of, but I see the elegance of just saying: "Your gradebook changed, so the gradebook definition has been deleted because it is not reliable anymore. You need to reconfigure your gradebook." It avoids the possibility of misrepresenting the gradebook as a perfect copy of the original. All that said - you can delete an assignment from a course, and categories will persist just fine. So I guess that answers my question: when you exclude a grade item from a course restore, the gradebook setup should behave the same way as when you delete a grade item from an existing course. Perhaps that needs to be specified more precisely, but it is a start. (I could probably shorten this post because I ended up answering my own question at the end, but I am leaving it all intact in case there is some value in showing my whole thought process. )

ResponsesInList.Title: 3.5 Grade Book & Bonus Marks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello We have a couple of instructors who want to add bonus marks to their grade books. The parent categories are set to weighted mean of grades (but have the option to be changed to Simple Weighted, Mean of Grades (with extra credits), and Natural.  We have tried all four options and the only one that seems to have the extra credit is Mean of Grades (with extra credits): We created a Bonus category using the Mean of Grades (with extra credits) and added a Grade item to that category. Settings for the item The category is set to exclude empty grades, which should discount anyone who didn't complete the bonus activity, but when we set the category weight to 2 (2% bonus mark), the overall mark for the students who submitted the bonus activity, seems to be skewed so they are being marked out of 100 instead of 102. If someone can identify where we have gone wrong, it would be very much appreciated. Thank you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 3.5 Grade Book & Bonus Marks
ResponsesInList.Text: The meaning of "extra credit" in Moodle is that when calculating percentages, the points from EC assignments are added to the numerator and not the denominator. If you want the students that submitted extra credit to be graded out of 102 instead of 100, then just add the assignment and don't add the extra credit designation. In the weighted grades scenario, the weight would be the amount above 100% a student could theoretically achieve if they score 100% on everything. For example, if I have an extra credit item in gradebook and weight it to "3", students could theoretically achieve 103% in the course. So, they would still be graded out of 100, but there are 3 extra points available. In other words, points added to the numerator but not the denominator. This is why students are being marked out of 100 instead of 102. If you want the students marked out of 102, just remove the extra credit designation. that makes it a normal assignment, not extra credit, or "bonus" in the sense that Moodle interprets it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 3.5 Grade Book & Bonus Marks
ResponsesInList.Text: If I understand your meaning of "bonus marks" as adding flat percentage points (i.e. final grade of 85.6% and a bonus mark of 2% would calculate to a truly final grade of 87.6%), then the only way I have found to accomplish this with my very limited experience is to: 1) Have the setup you have with the Bonus category weight of 0, and a bonus assignment within that category 2) Do a calculation on the final grade. Click edit on the course total (see attachment 1) Add ID Numbers and calculate the course total with the bonus (see attachment 2) example: ID " 1 " is for the exams with 40% weight, and so on.  ID 7 is the bonus and the weight of 1.25% is given.  You notice my weights add up to 101.25%. = 1 *0.4 + 2 *0.25 + 4 *0.15 + 5 *0.15 + 6 *0.05 + 7 *.0125 If we don't want the grade to go above 100%, then we can use: =if( #grade calculation# >100, 100, #grade calculation#) Hope this helps, Stuart
