Could someone help me figure it out how to make this formula in Moodle?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I make this formula?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am not sure there is an "IF" operator in Moodle calculations. Find the Moodle docs on all the operators here: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Grade_calculations I think I can help you get around this, but check to see you have done all of this first: First, you will need to make sure that your assignments have IDS for calculations. Do this by opening the calculation for the category or item you want to adjust: Then inputting the IDs you want to use in the boxes next to the relevant assignments: Click "add ID numbers and see that they have saved: Then use them to calculate the grade in the area above. Since we don't have an "IF" function, you may have to use a creative "max" or "min" function to achieve the same goal. For example, if you want to give the student the higher of the two results, you would calculate like this: =max((sum( FE ,average( A1 , A2 , A3 )))/2,average( A1 , A2 , A3 )) This may not be exactly what you're looking for, but it does achieve a similar objective without using "IF" and also using the syntax available to Moodle. My gradebook took it and it functions as expected, but I don't know if this is exactly what you're looking for. Mainly, try to rethink your goal without using IF.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I make this formula?
ResponsesInList.Text: I did it! Moodle 3.6 introduced the IF expression, I was using Moodle 3.4 and saw the 3.6 documentation which had the IF expression. This is the formula I used: =if( 4 >1,((average( 1 , 2 , 3 )+ 4 )/2),(average( 1 , 2 , 3 ))) Where 1, 2 and 3 are the normal grade items for all students and 4 is the final exam. This way, those students who received a grade in the final exam will have a specific formula for their final grade: (average( 1 , 2 , 3 )+ 4 )/2. And normal students will have their own formula as well: average( 1 , 2 , 3 )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook Conditional Calculations
ResponsesInList.Text:
basically you use the MIN and MAX functions to design factors that give back zero once your grade drops below a certain threshold. for example: total grade is 70% test grade and 30% presentation grade total grade should be negative if test score or presentation score are below 50 
```text
=(
test
*0.7+
presentation
*0.3)*max(min(floor(
test
)-49;1);0)*max(min(floor(
presentation
)-49;1);0)
```
 so after calculating our grade, we multiply it with our factors: 
```text
max(min(floor(
test
)-49;1);0)
```
 floor( test ) rounds it down to the next integer, so we don't have to deal with fractions then we subtract 49 from this number, so if the student had less than 50 points, we end up with zero then we take the minimum of what we end up with and 1, so the factor can never be more than 1 then we take the maximum of what we end up with and 0, so the factor can never be less than 0 thus, we have a factor that is 0 if the score for test was less than 50, and 1 if it was more than 50 - we multiply the whole grade with that factor, so if the student had less than 50 for the test, the whole grade is zero. this is very awkward and can get very complicated, however, as I just learned from this thread, apparently there are finally IF-statements for grade calculation in moodle in 3.6, which will make this a lot easier.

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading the number of activities completed
ResponsesInList.Text: In order to grade the degree of engagement of learners, I want add a grade category and award points depending on the number of (selected) activities completed in a course. I offer many optional "Extra" material (videos, texts, quizzies). Ideally it should be possible to selected the activities for which these extra points can be achieved. Example: 1-5 Extra activities completed => 'x' points 6-20 Extra activities completed => 'y' points ... Any suggestions on how to implement this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading the number of activities completed
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle 3.6: Create a gradebook with your activities in a category that uses natural aggregation, give the activities a grade value of 1, and set them up so that students will get that full 1 point for completing (how to do this varies by activity type). In the gradebook, weight the activities to "0" and create a grade item with whatever value you want to give ("x" in your post), below it is "5" in grade item "step 1": Edit "step 1" calculation: Give the activities item ids, below they are "AC1" "AC2" etc..., then input those item ids into this calculation =if(sum( AC1 , AC2 , AC3 , AC4 , AC5 , AC6 )>=5,5,0) and save. That will return the value "0" if the sum of the grade items is lower than 5 and the value "5" if the grade items are greater than or equal to 5. To award grade "y" in your post, repeat this process, adding another grade item with value "y-x" (where y-x equals 10 in the following calculation) and the calculation =if(sum( AC1 , AC2 , AC3 , AC4 , AC5 , AC6 )>=10,10,0) In Moodle 3.5 and below There is no "if" function. I'm working on how to work around that. I'll update later.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 3.5 Gradebook landing page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Susan, If you're referring to the link in the Course Administration block, then take note that there have been a few changes. Prior to Moodle 3, there was only a "Gradebook" link in the Admin block, which went to the Grader Report for teachers and the User Report for students. For students, this was the link they'd see in the Administration block. Since Moodle 3.0 or 3.1, there were 2 links in the Admin block: the Gradebook (Grader Report) and a new link - the Gradebook Set Up. As of Moodle 3.4, the "Gradebook" link is now in the Navigation block (for BOTH teachers and students). All that remains in the Administration block is the Gradebook Set Up link. It may not make as much sense from a teacher standpoint, but from a student standpoint it is a improvement in the sense that there is one less block in their course. Now when students are in a course they don't have a random "Administration" block with simply just a 'gradebook' link. The Navigation block is a better location because that's where the other course specific links are located (badges, participants, etc...). The only issue I find with the Navigation block is that it's a gazillion miles long. There are different course formats (such as Fordson) that attempt to put frequently used links in a quick access area... You could also add an HTML block in your course with a link to the GraderReport if that helps in the meantime... I just wanted to write so you understood the gradual change over the past few Moodle versions and that this probably will not 'change back' to how it was before.

ResponsesInList.Text: Competencies and Grades are not related items in Moodle. They are independent methods of assessing learning and/or skills. IMHO - they should be related. As an instructor, using Moodle gradebook allows you the flexibility to adjust (re-grade) a student. Competencies are earned or deleted, you cannot change the "rating". If you created competency scales such as; White Belt, Yellow Belt, Orange Belt, Green Belt, Blue Belt, Purple Belt, Brown Belt and Black Belt. Once a student earns their White Belt, you cannot change the student's rating to Yellow Belt. There is also no standard reporting for competencies and learning plans. I would probably consider changing my gradebrook letter values to the desired competency level. 0-10 points = White Belt, 11- 20 = Yellow Belt, or whatever points/scale method meets your needs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Find EVERYTHING that needs grading? MSSQL query
ResponsesInList.Text: I have just come across this question while I did search for an answer to that. I have designed a query which will help you to find the list of the assignment submitted required grading... I hope someone can be benefited and any improvement to the query is most welcome... SELECT [Course URL ] ,[Course Full Name] ,[Course Short Name] ,[Assignment Title] ,[Assignment Type] ,[Due Date] ,[Student Name] ,[Submission Status] ,[Time Submitted] ,CASE WHEN MonthDiff < 0 THEN FORMAT(ABS(MonthDiff),'Late Submission 0 month(s)') WHEN WeekDiff < 0 THEN FORMAT(ABS(WeekDiff),'Late Submission 0 week(s)') WHEN DayDiff < 0 THEN FORMAT(ABS(DayDiff),'Late Submission 0 day(s)') WHEN HourDiff < 0 THEN FORMAT(ABS(HourDiff),'Late Submission 0 hour(s)') WHEN MinDiff < 0 THEN FORMAT(ABS(MinDiff),'Late Submission 0 minute(s)') ELSE 'Submitted On Time' END SubmissionOnTime ,'' Grade FROM ( SELECT ' https://qmplus.qmul.ac.uk/course/view.php?id=' + FORMAT(c.id,'0') [Course URL] ,c.fullname [Course Full Name] ,c.shortname [Course Short Name] ,ass.name [Assignment Title] ,IIF(LEN(CAST(ast.value as NVARCHAR(MAX))) > 0, UPPER(ast.plugin) + ' (' + CAST(ast.value as NVARCHAR(MAX)) + ')', UPPER(ast.plugin)) [Assignment Type] ,DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01') AS [Due Date] ,u.firstname + ' ' + u.lastname [Student Name] ,asb.[status] [Submission Status] ,CASE WHEN asb.status = 'submitted' THEN  DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01') ELSE NULL END AS [Time Submitted] ,DATEDIFF(MONTH,DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01'), DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01')) MonthDiff ,DATEDIFF(WEEK,DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01'), DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01')) WeekDiff ,DATEDIFF(DAY,DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01'), DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01')) DayDiff ,DATEDIFF(HOUR,DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01'), DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01')) HourDiff ,DATEDIFF(MINUTE,DATEADD(s, asb.timemodified, '1970-01-01'), DATEADD(s, ass.duedate, '1970-01-01')) MinDiff FROM prefix_user u LEFT JOIN prefix_user_enrolments ue ON u.id = ue.userid LEFT JOIN prefix_enrol e ON ue.enrolid = e.id LEFT JOIN prefix_course c ON e.courseid = c.id LEFT JOIN prefix_assign ass ON c.id = ass.course AND ass.duedate > 0 AND ass.duedate < DATEDIFF(SECOND, '1970-01-01', GETDATE()+365) LEFT JOIN prefix_assign_submission AS asb ON ass.id = asb.assignment AND u.id = asb.userid AND asb.latest = 1 INNER JOIN prefix_course_modules cm ON ass.id = cm.instance AND c.id = cm.course LEFT JOIN ( SELECT DISTINCT g.finalgrade AS value, u.id AS userid, i.iteminstance AS assignmentID, cm.module FROM prefix_grade_items AS i INNER JOIN prefix_grade_grades AS g ON i.id = g.itemid INNER JOIN prefix_user AS u ON g.userid = u.id INNER JOIN prefix_course_modules cm ON i.iteminstance = cm.instance AND i.courseid = cm.course AND cm.module = 38 AND i.itemmodule = 'assign' WHERE g.finalgrade IS NOT NULL AND g.hidden = 0 AND i.display = 0 AND cm.visible = 1 ) g ON cm.instance = g.assignmentID AND cm.module = g.module AND u.id = g.userid LEFT JOIN prefix_assign_plugin_config ast ON ass.id = ast.assignment AND ast.subtype = 'assignsubmission' AND ast.name = 'filetypeslist' WHERE asb.status = 'submitted' AND g.value IS NULL ) a ORDER BY [Assignment Title], [Student Name]

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook taking too much memory to run
ResponsesInList.Text: It still can take a while in large enrollment courses, but we found that boosting max allowed packets for the database was the most significant positive step we tried. We actually had a course locked up after a teacher did a grade recalculation and this change was what got that course accessible and allowed it to finish up the task. You can try this even as a temporary setting since you can update that one without a server restart (dynamic). The maximum setting is 1073741824, but make sure you have plenty of RAM if you go that high (32GB or more). You may find that this setting boost will also help with restoring to a new course in those courses with large question banks and lots of quizzes. We also found that increasing max_heap-table_size and tmp_table_size was a big help. Those are also settings you can try without a server restart. Just remember that if those setting changes do end up helping that you set them temporarily. They will go away in the next server restart. If they help, make them permanent by changing them in my.cnf set global max_heap_table_size =33554432 set global tmp_table_size = 33554432 set global max_allowed_packet=1073741824 I recommend increasing your setting slowly, but the above values are what we finally settled on since we do have really large question bank courses (5,000 to 10,000 questions) and large enrollment courses (many hundreds of students). We might be able to lower them now. We found out that our remote host accidentally set us up on a file system that had been deprecated. We were on that server two years all the while boosting settings to try to help with those large processes. When they caught their error and moved us to a server with the current file system, we found many things ran much faster. I have not explored if we now can set those settings lower and get as good a result. We definitely needed them on the original server though.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Gradebook with Weighted Mean of Grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mike We find that if you set your weightings to reflect your percentages, then the totals are usually accurate.  Alternately, find your lowest denominator and use that for your weightings: Quizzes = 20% of the final grade - 2 weight - twice the lowest value Assignments = 10% of the final grade - 1 weight - lowest value; everything else becomes a factor Project = 25% of the final grade - 2.5 weight - two and a half more than the lowest value Exams = 40% of the final grade. - 4 weight - four times the lowest value Note, you can also use half values; example 5% might translate in this instance to a weight of .5 Hope this helps, Susan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do you determine the BEST STUDENT of a programme when the time is right?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am answering my own question after eight days. Haha. I solved this. The trick is to use the Configurable reports block (plugin) . For your convenience, I reproduce the SQL Query code in the text below: SELECT prefix_course.id AS courseid, prefix_course.shortname AS Course_ShortName, prefix_user.id AS studentid, prefix_user.firstname AS FirstName, prefix_user.lastname AS LastName, prefix_grade_grades.finalgrade AS coursetotalgrade FROM prefix_grade_grades JOIN prefix_user ON prefix_grade_grades.userid = prefix_user.id JOIN prefix_grade_items ON prefix_grade_grades.itemid = prefix_grade_items.id JOIN prefix_course ON prefix_grade_items.courseid = prefix_course.id WHERE prefix_grade_items.itemtype = 'course'AND prefix_user.lastname='GIJB Jan 2016' ORDER BY prefix_course.idnumber, prefix_user.username, prefix_grade_items.itemname, prefix_grade_grades.timemodified Note: replace  the line prefix_user.lastname='GIJB Jan 2016' with your own values between the apostrophes. Clicking the "View report" tab (which is to the immediate left of "Custom SQL") of the block tab yields this output for me: I then save the output as an Excel export file. The rest is manual work on the Excel to give me enough information as to who is the top scorer. Hope this helps someone.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Competency and grades are two different things. Competencies are linked to Learning Plans (and Learning Plans Templates) Competencies must be created in a competency framework, linked to a course and then can be linked to the desired course activity. The students competencies are displayed on a Learning Plan block, not on a Course Completion report and not in the gradebook. If you set up the Competencies and Learning Plans the students who have not completed the training activity will be displayed without a status. The Not Yet Competent scale value is not displayed. The Competent scale will be displayed to the students. I recommend that you review the Moodle documentation for Learning Plans and Competencies .

ResponsesInList.Title: Unentered Grades in Calculation are Zero
ResponsesInList.Text: For the exams grade, if my students improve from the midterm to the final, I weight them differently: 25%-midterm and 75%-final instead of 50-50.  Unfortunately, when I use this formula, it counts the final as zero, so for most of the semester, the exam grade is really low. The formula is: =max(average( midterm , final ), ( midterm + 3 * final )/4) Is there any way to fix this so that it just uses the midterm grade without me having to change the formula later on?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unentered Grades in Calculation are Zero
ResponsesInList.Text: You might consider making a "helper" grade item, that you would use in your formula instead of `final`. The helper grade item would be hidden, and set to have a weight of 0 (so that it does not appear to students, and does not contribute to their overall grade). That grade item formula could use a clever combination of ROUND, FLOOR, CEILING, MIN, MAX, 1, and/or 0, to basically return the `midterm` value of the `final` is 0, or otherwise return the `final` value. Then, the non-weighted or weighted average of `midterm` with itself, is exactly `midterm`. (of course, you do not necessarily need to make it a separate grade item, you could just repeatedly substitute the helper calculation into your formula. However, if you're going to repeat a calculation , I would prefer to put it somewhere else.) Notice the problem with that, though: based on the way calculations work with empty grades, there is no way to distinguish an empty grade, from a 0 grade. So, the resulting `exams` grade will be wrong if a student legitimately scores a 0 on the final . The workaround would be that you just manually override the grade for anyone who scores a 0 (and outside Moodle, encourage them to score higher than a 0 in the future, at least for the sake of your calculations ). If you can guarantee that all students' grades are non-zero , then the formulae in this thread (or this thread ) might suggest a way to count if a grade exists or not. That might allow you to completely forgo all this "helper" stuff. Another example of a logical formula includes this "fixed score" method in the Moodle Docs . Do either of those options sound helpful? - Ray

This topic is about the displaying of unenrolled users that got some grades and I first describe some of our use cases. Perquisites: At our institution (a university) a teacher can apply for a Moodle course for his lecture. Then students who want to attend the lecture can self-enrol into the course. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: False result with letters, but correct result with points?
ResponsesInList.Text: Rein, You are making a mistake with what the numerical values of the scale are. The first value of the scale is 0. F,E,D,C,B,A is not 1,2,3,4,5,6 but 0,1,2,3,4,5. Therefore the equation in your first example is: (3/5*30 + 2/5*20 + 25/50*50) / (30 + 20 + 50) = .51 = 51% = 51/100 Go into the "Course grade settings" and set "Grade display type"  to "Real (percentage)" and you can confirm this. If you really want an F to be 1 point and an A to be 6, then use something like 0,F,E,D,C,B,A as your scale.

ResponsesInList.Title: Excluding restricted items
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, It has been some time I am trying to find a suitable setting for graded items that are restricted. In a course module we have: Activity 1a OR Activity 1b AND Activity 2 Activities 1a - 1b are restricted to each other. If student takes 1a, the 1b will hide and vise versa. Activity 1 (a OR b) worth 50% Activity 2 worth 50% as well. So if student Z gains full marks in Activity 1a and Activity 2 the total score of the module should be 100%. If student Z gains full marks in Activity 1a but not take Activity 2 the module total should be 50% too. The problem here is that in gradebook if I exclude empty grades I get the correct total as far it concerns 1a - 1b, but wrong total as far it concerns Activity 1 and 2. Doesn't sound reasonable graded activities that are restricted to be automatically excluded from gradebook aggregations? As there is a setting in gradebook to hide hidden items from the gradebook, shouldn't be a setting to exclude hidden items from aggregation? Exclude empty grades is not the same with exclude hidden (restricted) items . In the above example if student X takes only Activity 1a, Activities 1b and Activity 2 are treated the same from the system, while they are not. Activity 1b is hidden due to course restrictions (users can take either 1a either 1b) and Activity 2 is an empty grade. Calculations is the only option I see here, yet not my favourite. I would appreciate if anyone has a better idea. kan

ResponsesInList.Title: Achievement Charts + Moodle Gradebook (looking for suggestions)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello, I wish I could keep this post short, but there's quite a lot to consider here and, to be frank, I'm having a hard time nailing down my own thoughts on this issue. Here’s the challenge: How can we incorporate an Achievement
Chart into a Moodle course so that it works like this: https://www.screencast.com/t/c5hkaqNk ? Some background: In our province, the Ministry of Education requires that course
assessments/evaluations are built around the KICA categories of achievement, which is a
standard province-wide guide used by all teachers as a framework to assess and
evaluate student achievement. KICA = Knowledge, Inquiry, Communication, Application Here’s an example:  Let’s
assume that the course ENGLISH10 is using the following KICA distribution for the entire
course: 30% Knowledge 20% Inquiry 40% Communication 10% Application This means that, cumulatively, when all KICA values from ALL the activities are added up (and weights are applied), they should reflect the overall KICA distribution. Of course, this does not mean that all individual activities use the
same KICA distribution as the overall course KICA targets. An individual activity in ENGLISH10 could have the KiCA values of
30%-0%-50%-20%, for example. Moreover, the weighting of the KICA categories is separate from the weighting of the gradebook categories. Some things to consider: The gradebook categories can’t
be used for this purpose because: Gradebook categories are used
to weigh activities based on the general grade-breakdown scheme, which is
separate from KICA, as shown here: https://www.screencast.com/t/c5hkaqNk Even if the gradebook
categories were used for this purpose, KICA categories are not compatible with
gradebook categories since single activities need to be associated with
multiple KICA categories (in the Moodle gradebook an activity can only belong
to one category). In essence, I think we need a way of combining the Gradebook
categories and the KICA categories. The Marking Guide option ( https://www.screencast.com/t/pDovWg8tJn )  might conceivably do the trick (though I haven't thought it out) but Marking Guides can’t
be applied to quizzes. What the teacher needs: A way to set KICA values in any
activity (+ a way to set weights to KICA categories) A way to check student progress
according to KICA categories (ex. Johnny’s currently Communication score is 65%) A grades report that shows how KICA
categories and Gradebook categories are combined to generate grades (how did Johnny get that grade?) What students need: A way to see how their grades
are determined by combining KICA and Gradebook category weights. So there you have it. I'm stumped. I've developed a mock-up to create a KICA plugin but it's quite cumbersome and not very elegant, so I don't want to pursue it until I exhaust different options. Wondering it anyone has suggestions or different approaches  to this challenge? Thanks for your time, Fernando

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Achievement Charts + Moodle Gradebook (looking for suggestions)
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you looked at competencies?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Achievement Charts + Moodle Gradebook (looking for suggestions)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the suggestion, Emma. ASAIK, competencies can't be used as a grading framework. The way I see it, and I could be off here, to use KICA in the grading framework, we'd need a way to apply a secondary weighting system to the gradebook setup page. A tall order, to be sure. These type of achievement charts are pretty common, at least here in Canada. I wonder how (if!) other schools manage to do it in Moodle. I suspect this done as an extra step outside Moodle via spreadsheets and/or 3rd party gradebook programs. Cheers, Fernando

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 3.3: Grade aggregation issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! I am having an issue with grade book aggregation in Moodle 3.3.  I am a design specialist, and I know what I want our courses to do, but I am not a computer programmer. I am providing a link to this post for a system admin to also follow. We have over a hundred course shells on our server and several thousand students. Here is the issue: We need an accurate current grade to report for students that are moving at varying paces through the course.  Flexible pace students need to be able to work ahead and have their grade calculate accurately even if other students are working behind them. All students, both traditional and flexible pace, need to have a zero reported for empty grades once the due date has passed. We function on quarterly grading periods with a semester exam and semester final grade. We have created categories for each quarter and the exams.  We use calculated grade items to report these overall grades to our student information system. Our quarterly categories include a main folder of all assignments for that quarter with blanks not included in the calculation. We recently added a sub category folder for when an assignment deadline passes, teachers move items there and blanks will count as zeros.  The goal is to allow students working ahead to see their grade, but not penalize students on pace. We have tried various aggregations, and two have been the most promising, but neither work exactly the way we need. Option 1: Quarter Category Folder = Simple Weighted Mean of grades; this provides an overall percentage to report to our grade calculation column for the SIS. Sub category (Graded Assignments) = Natural aggregation (this prevents the folder from inaccurately weighting the grades that are placed into it.) Problem: there is a miscalculation in the parent category folder for the assignments ranging from .5%-5% maybe greater. Option 2: Quarter Category Folder = Natural; this resolves the issue in Option 1 and the percentage calculates correctly. Problem: the calculated grade item column that reports to our SIS only shows the running total of points and not a percentage which is what our students and clients need to see there. I have added a PDF of screen shots for a better view. Considerations: We use a calculation of = 1-9wk for the first nine weeks column to pull the total from that folder. I can't think of a hard calculation to use there since the running total of points changes for students depending on their pace. We discovered that the User report was showing the correct calculation for the nine weeks category folder because we had a setting at the admin level to not include hidden grades.  When we changed that the user report then matched the teacher report which is unfortunately the wrong calculation.  I have looked everywhere for a hidden assignment that might be causing this.  None to be found.

I am largely a fan of systems of record that are dedicated to that purpose, however that doesn't always serve us in the trenches. One thought I had here in reflection was that if you left out the grade (as a percentage or letter) and shifted to a notion of competencies, this is what the Competencies tool supports by design. A more permanent record of my achievement in a Competency stored on the user rather than the course gradebook. I can see my achievements from prior work as they align against specific Competencies, and I can use that in a learning plan construct to see how far I have come and how much needs to go. It isn't exactly what you've asked for here, but perhaps with a little shift it could be a good fit for your needs or others who are contemplating the similar goals.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recalculating grades - FATAL ERROR
ResponsesInList.Text: As was pointed out above, the problem is that custom calculations that are invalid now cause an infinite loop of 'recalculating'. This can happen if you have a custom calculation, and then you delete an activity that is used in that custom calculation. We currently get around it by finding the course grade item in grade_items, and settings needsupdate to 0. Then you can access the gradebook editor edit the bad calculation. I'm opening a MDL ticket for it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recalculating grades - FATAL ERROR
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! We were able to fix the problem without directly editing the database - that makes me nervous doing that on our now very active Moodle since classes have started. You will need the courseid number - which is the end number when viewing the main page of a class site page - for example: https://yourMoodleURL/course/view.php?id=2818 For the example here, the courseid number is 2818 The you will need to find the id value of the item for the custom grade calculation. For this, I used a mysql command to get the information I needed: SELECT * FROM `mdl_grade_items` WHERE `courseid` = 2818 AND `needsupdate` = 1; After all the field names listed and a bunch of lines you should see two numbers - something like this: | 4789 |     2818 | where the first number is the id and the second is the courseid number - in this example the id is 4789 With this information use the folowing URL to go directly to the custom grade item: https:// yourMoodleURL /grade/edit/tree/ calculation.php?courseid= 2818 & id= 4789 &gpr_type=edit&gpr_ plugin=tree&gpr_courseid= 2818 where you would place in your corresponding numbers for the courseid and id Hope this makes sense and is useful. Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: i dont want to give 100% to my students if they answer all the 10questions right
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a grade book question so I am moving to that forum.  You are going to need a custom calculation for the second quiz.  Or perhaps the two quizzes need to be in a category and then the category needs the custom calculation - that might work better.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: i dont want to give 100% to my students if they answer all the 10questions right
ResponsesInList.Text: Quiz settings allow you to customize what feedback they get (overall feedback and review options).  You decide what they get. Grade boundary in overall feedback should be just below the actual boundary...so my quizzes have a 70% expectation, my boundary is 69.99%.  I add the .99% because some of my questions have partially correct answers and someone could get 69.5% and still not pass but get passing feedback if the boundary is 69% ('cuz their score is higher than 69%, if only by .5%). You don't want them to see their points/percentage, turn points off in review options. And as for grade book display...you can always hide it or set it to letter grades and then modify the letter grade rubric.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I display "Category and Items"? How do I display the Grade Item edit icon?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Teacher Emma, (Version 3.0.8) Many thanks again for helping me! Thank you for your attention and for your patience! I apologize for the delay in responding to your message and thanking you for your precious explanations. Thank you very much! After your precious help I was able to perform several actions within the GradeBook. And I would like to leave a little tutorial, if there are others like me, who do not understand the GradeBook well, can guide you to understand it. This is how I have done the actions within the GradeBook: 1- To act on "Grade Category", "Grade Item" and on Activities : 1.1- Enter Moodle and then click on the course 1.2- Go to: Course Management >> GradeBook Configuration 2- To delete a Grade Category : Click on the "Edit" menu and then "Delete" All elements within the "Grade Category" will be deleted, with the exception of activities. To delete activities: Activate the edit and then on the activity menu click on "Edit" and then click delete. Always be careful to delete any items. 3- To add a multiplying factor: Go to the activity where you want to put the multiplier and click on the "Edit" menu of the activity. On the new screen, click on "Show More" and the location for the multiplying factor will appear. 4-To unlock "Grade Category", "Grade Item" and Activities: It can be done like this: 4.1- Within GradeBook Configuration, change to "Grade Report" in the box in the drop-down menu. 4.2- Click on "Activate Editing" 4.3- Note that there is an item called "controls", follow your line and see that on each element ("Grade Item", Activities and etc.) there are a number of small icons. Move the mouse over each of them to find out the function they perform. 4.4- To unlock, simply click on the "lock" of the item to be unlocked. 4.5- There is a hierarchy, so if the "Grade Category" is blocked, to unlock any elements within it, first unlock the "Grade Category", then act on the other elements within it. 4.6 - If there are calculations involving some other "Grade Item", this other one also needs to be unblocked. Thank you very much! Marcelo.

ResponsesInList.Text: Our courses have a simple assessment structure Each course has a number of assignments. Each assignment is graded as Complete/Not Complete All assignments must be Complete for the course to be passed. What is the best way to set this up? Should I use the lowest grade aggregation type with no empty grades? Do I need to set up the Complete/Not Complete scale? Moodle 3.1

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting up simple grading
ResponsesInList.Text: You can use the completion tracking feature of Moodle. step 1: Go to site administration > Advanced features > click the check box for "Enable completion tracking" > click on save changes. Step 2 : Go to your course > edit settings > Completion tracking > choose "yes" for "Enable completion tracking". step 3: Go to each activities of course > edit settings > Activity completion > choose criteria what you want > save changes. step 4: Again go to course administration > Course completion > configure your completion settings > save changes. Useful Links:- https://docs.moodle.org/23/en/Course_completion_settings https://docs.moodle.org/27/en/Activity_completion_settings Regards, Purnendu

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to enable Simple View and Full View in Moodle - Version 3.0.8 ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Teacher Emma, I'm sorry for the delay in replying. Yes, there are 3 deadlines in an activity: First - Period of time, where the student needs to send their files. Second - Activity correction period - Starts when the 1st ends Third - Sending the notes to the University System - Starts when the 2nd ends Procedures: 1- When the activity correction time ends, the activity is blocked by the Course Secretary and the file is sent to the University System. 1.1- Before activities were blocked by the Course Secretary, there were often situations where tutors delayed corrections. With this, there were cases in which the Course Secretary sent the notes to the University System and after this occurred, tutors corrected the activities and sent the students' notes to Moodle. As a result students got Zero grade in the University System. 1.2- Currently, the Course Secretariat blocks activities after the end of the correction period. This ensures that the file uploaded to the University System reflects exactly what is in Moodle. 1.3- The tutors who delay the sending of notes, will have to do it by e-mail to the Course Secretary. With these data, the Coordination of the Curso can act on the tutors who delay the sending of the notes and protect the students, so that they do not leave without notes in the System of the University. 2- There is another situation where note blending occurs. It is as follows: 2.1- There are activities that require the teacher of the discipline, follow closely, even guiding, as the tutors must correct. There are several cases, in which the notes given by the tutors, are outside the criterion, previously established by the teachers. With this there were complaints from the students and the tutors changed the grades up. Most of these modifications did not meet the correction criteria, informed by the teachers of the discipline. With this, the teachers of the discipline, block the activity, preventing tutors from throwing wrong notes in Moodle (very up). There are many tutor exchanges and it is not always possible to keep a team with experience. Many thanks, teacher Emma! Marcelo.

Our students are very confused by the current gradebook since it will show them as having an F until quite close to the end of the course since its grading is cumulative. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to show both "exclude empty grades" and "include empty grades" simultaneously in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the majority of us exclude empty grades and give zeros for missed assignments...I just think this would add a layer of complexity when we are really trying to simplify the gradebook. But, that is simply my opinion...maybe some others will weigh in here.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to show both "exclude empty grades" and "include empty grades" simultaneously in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Evan The option to include or exclude empty grades is based on the Gradebook categories so if you wanted to have both you could add another category and have the option ticked or not and include the appropriate grade items. As mentioned though this is adding a layer of complexity to the gradebook which maybe difficult to manage depending on the number of Courses. Either way an explanation to students should be clear in that their final grade is an interim grade until all course assessment items have been submitted (or not) and they need to look at the overall assessments and the weightings (if used) when looking at the course grade. So to do the opposite as you have you put a tick in the parent category to 'exclude empty grades' which then shows the student their current course grade based on the assignments they have submitted. This of course could show the student has a HD but in fact the last assessment item has a weighting of say 60% and say they get a pass for this one there overall grade would drop. Personally I prefer the latter as it gives a 'current state' of the overall grade but it does mean that students may look at this and 'slack off' for the last assessment because they only need a pass to get over the line in the course. I think it's well worth setting up Course Completion also so they see that they need to complete all activities to pass a course. Unfortunately Course completion data and Final Grades aren't linked. Hope the above helps in what is a mind field!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overview of all grades in different courses for one student
ResponsesInList.Text:
You can try the Configurable Reports plugin ( https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=block_configurable_reports ). After installing it add the Configurable Reports block to your front page (and/or My Moodle page, if you use it). Then use a query like the following to produce a report for each student that shows all their results across all their courses: 
```text
SELECT


 u.firstname AS 'First',


 u.lastname AS 'Last',


 u.firstname + ' ' + u.lastname AS 'Display Name',


 c.fullname AS 'Course',


 cc.name AS 'Category',


 CASE


  WHEN gi.itemtype = 'course' THEN c.fullname + ' Course Total'


  ELSE gi.itemname


  END AS 'Item Name',
```
 The important part in that query is: 
```text
%%USERID%%
```
 That variable translates to the user id of the student that is logged into Moodle, so each student sees just his or her own "report". You can change the SQL above to create any type of report you can imagine... More info: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/view.php?id=7979 https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=block_configurable_reports The Custom SQL Queries Report is just as powerful. See https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=report_customsql and https://docs.moodle.org/27/en/Custom_SQL_queries_report for more info.

The code is using all grade items, although the comment says "this is to adjust the total for the particular user" but no totalisation is done in the main loop, 4. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How Does the Grade book Calculate Grades?
ResponsesInList.Text: I believe the gradebook is adjusting because there are some items that have not been attempted yet that have a weight to them.  So for the purpose of the grade right now, the gradebook is showing how much weight that category carried towards the grade at hand.  Because Final Group projects are excluded, it would make sense that their weights were excluded to.  Otherwise, students could never receive over 85% until the final project was completed. As to comparing with their excel sheet, without knowing how they calculated that, it is hard to tell.  The gradebook will divide total points possible by total points attained to reach the percentage (then multiplied by weight if weighted).  I have had teachers report that before and have always been able to get the gradebook within a percent of their calculations (sometimes rounding up skews off just a hair) - normally, it is a mistake in the gradebook setup.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting a Scale from Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi there As Elena indicated you'll need to query the database to find this information. First you need to know the id number of the scale. Check this in the mdl_scale table with a query similar to this (alternatively just select * from mdl_scale to get all rows!): 
```text
select id, name, scale from mdl_scale where name = 'name of scale';
```
 Once you have the id number of the scale (say it's '10') you can search the msl_grade_items table for the items using that scale with a query similar to this: 
```text
select id, courseid, itemname, scaleid from mdl_grade_items where scaleid=10;
```
 Once you've gone through those courses and changed the grade item's scale to something else you should be able to remove the scale. I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

Go to edit settings of grade item. See for the option grade type grade type it is set to scale, make it value. Now go to scale, now you can delete the scale showing status used:No.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting a Scale from Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Re: Is there a way I can see where the scale is being used (without having to go in every course and check each assignment etc)? It's many years since this question was first posed but I had the same issue today. I resolved it using the Configurable Reports plugin and the following SQL Query: 
```text
SELECT prefix_course.fullname AS Course, prefix_course.shortname AS "Course Short Name", prefix_grade_items.itemname AS "Graded Item Name", prefix_grade_items.itemmodule AS "Graded Item Type" 

FROM  prefix_grade_items

INNER JOIN prefix_course 

ON prefix_grade_items.courseid=prefix_course.id

WHERE prefix_grade_items.scaleid="[SCALE ID NUMBER]"
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should suspended users appear in the gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry to sound a dissenting note, but I am not sure. It all depends what we mean by 'Suspended' users. 1. The interpretation one might deduce from MDL-26373 is that suspending a user is the right way to temporarily prevent them from coming in to the course. 2. A user whose enrolment has been suspended is effectively un-enrolled from the course. In Moodle 2.0, if you unenrol a user, then all the data about that user in the course, including grades, should be deleted. Therefore, if you care about keep complete records, or if you are worried about making a mistake, and would like unenrolling a user to be undoable, then you can never use un-enrol. You should always suspend the enrolment instead. (That is also advice given by Petr Skoda, who is giving the advice about the use of suspend in MDL-26373 above.) In you believe 1., then having the suspended users appear in the gradebook, but styled different is right. If you believe 2. Then suspended users should not appear in the gradebook. I'm afraid I think that both these cases are important. There must be a way to temporarily suspend a user's access to the course, and there must be a way to effectively unenrol a user that does not cause dataloss. Therefore, there is not a good answer in the gradebook. Make it configurable is a feeble answer. A proper answer is probably to work on the enrolment data-model, so that it can correctly capture the difference between 1. and 2., but that is a lot of work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restricting Teachers to viewing their own students grades ONLY
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to go into the course settings, and under Groups > Group Mode, select Separate Groups. This setting has 3 options: No groups - There are no sub groups, everyone is part of one big community Separate groups - Each group member can only see their own group, others are invisible Visible groups - Each group member works in their own group, but can also see other groups The group mode defined at course level is the default mode for all activities within the course. Each activity that supports groups can also define its own group mode, though if the group mode is forced at course level, the group mode setting for each activity is ignored. --- Then in Site Administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles, you can tweak your Teacher persmissions (I searched for "all" to make sure teachers didn't see all grades for instance) Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Setting grade scale help
ResponsesInList.Text: I am new to using Moodle and our company is starting to use it. We are a corporate company and not a school. We have hundreds of internal pages of documentation that deal with different types of software that we use. We are creating courses for teaching that software to employees and need to evaluate their progress. Moodle 3 is installed and the migration from our Intranet is in progress. Here is my current way of grading: Currently I grade the employees that took the courses like this: 1 - competent 2 - doing ok 3 - just ok 4 - not doing well at all I was (am still) using a spread sheet to calculate the grades. Let's say I have a course that has 5 tutorials that need graded. This student, Andrew, was marked like this: Tutorial 1 = 1 Tutorial 2 =  2 Tutorial 3 = 1 Tutorial 4 = 1 Tutorial 5 = 1 The formula I am using is this: =SUM(G5;G33;G58;G81;G104) which equals a score of 6 for Andrew. I then use this formula to derive his grade: =INT(100*(5/6) which gives me a grade of 83 out of 100 If he were to get all "1's" then his grade would have been 100. Sorry for the long explanation but I wanted to show how I grade currently. Now for my question: Is there a why or how would I set up the same type of 4 tiered grades to have the Grade Book calculate grades based on what I am currently doing. Is that even possible. Thank you for any input or help that you might have. Dennis

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting grade scale help
ResponsesInList.Text: I figured it out. Here is the solution: Use Natural for the Category Then add this formula into the Calculation field: =5/SUM( T1 , T2 , T4 , T5 , T5 )*100 So, there are 5 items to grade and divided by the sum of the grades, which gives me .8333 multiplied by 100 The final grade is printed as 83.33 Then turn on Letter (percentage) in the Grade display type and you get this: B (83.33%) Just took some rethinking on how to get it work. dennis

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting grade scale help
ResponsesInList.Text: If you reverse the order of your scale, putting the worst first and the best last, you get values 4..1, rather than 1..4.  Your maximum possible result is then 5*4, which is the divisor of the sum of marks. =sum(T1,T2,T3,T4,T5)/4*5*100 This actually gives you monotonically decreasing values down to the minimum of 25%. 1, .95, .9 ... .35, .3, .25 So Andrew would get 95%, rather than 83.3%. Your calculation gives a distorted set of values. 1, 0.833, 0.714, 0.625 ... 0.294, 0.277, 0.263, 0.25 Notice the spread of differences at the top and bottom of the scale.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting grade scale help
ResponsesInList.Text: And it occurs to me that you can get the desired effect without changing the scale (although changing the scale would be best) by converting each value with abs(val - 5) which would convert 1..4 into 4..1.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting grade scale help
ResponsesInList.Text: Make that =sum(T1,T2,T3,T4,T5)/(4*5)*100

ResponsesInList.Title: timecreated is null in mdl_grade_grades after grading submission
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle 2.5 I added an assignment, logged in as a student and added a submission. I looked in mdl_grade_grades table and saw that the timecreated field had a time stamp.  I initially thought timecreated was for when a record was added to the table. I went back into the assignment as a teacher and graded the submission, when I looked at mdl_grade_grades table I saw the timecreated field changed to null and the timemodifed field had a timestamp. I was looking through the code and noticed the following call stack: - mod/assign/locallib.php - gradebook_item_update() calls convert_grade_for_gradebook() where datesubmitted is set to null.  Lastly it calls mod/assign/lib.php - calls assign_grade_item_update(), passing the data structure where datesubmitted is null - mod/assign/lib.php - assign_grade_Item_update() calls lib/gradelib.php - grade_update() passing the data structure where datesubmitted is null - lib/gradelib.php - grade_update() calls lib/grade/grade_item.php - update_raw_grade() passing datesubmitted as an argument - lib/grade/grade_item.php - update_raw_grade() sets the grade_grades instance timecreated property to datesubmitted (null).  The docblock stating "$datesubmitted A timestamp of when the student's work was submitted", but it's value is set to null. This seems like a bug but wanted to get some input on this to see if there was an undocumented reason. I came across this because I had a teacher user giving an assignment grade for a student that never added a submission; thought the timecreated field in the mdl_grade_grades was null to denote the user never actually submitted anything.  Unfortunately this is always the case no matter the scenario.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Modify grade item weight for a single student

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resetting all overridden flags
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Natalie, Assuming you have phpMyAdmin , you can reset all the overridden flags as follows: Click the SQL tab, then in the "Run SQL query/queries on database moodle" field type UPDATE mdl_grade_grades SET overridden = 0 and click the Go button. Please note that it's always a good idea to make a backup of your database before trying any SQL queries. If you think it would be helpful to have a setting within Moodle for resetting all overridden flags, please create an issue for it in the tracker.

ResponsesInList.Text: I believe that I cured the problem. Working in a test copy of the course, I set all the weights to 0  in the Grader Report/Gradebook set up. All categories and the course total are now 0. When I export to Excel, they are 0 and now my calculation will work without all the hassle of removing columns or unchecking options just before I export to Excel. To answer your first question: I dropped the K-12 Weighted Grading system for something that is much more real world qualifying.  I give points as grades.  Depending on the number of graded activities I give, students can earn around 4000 points for their work. One assignment can have a value of 37 maximum points for a job well done while part of the term project can earn 739 points.  One could call it weighting, but it is not based  on that archaic 100% idea. I was always amused that the value that is used in the calculation of the category total is not based on the value you select in a scale.  It is based on the number of entries in the scale.  For example, if I have a scale of even numbers {0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14} Moodle sees 7 for the calculations because the are 8 (compensating for 0" entries in the scale. I red a thread here, or somewhere else, about this and it set me to thinking. Anyway, the Category and Course total issue has been solved.....

ResponsesInList.Title: How to handle resit marks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi O' Gradebook Pro and Most Enlightened One I have a problem to solve. At the moment, the only way I know that I can handle resit marks is to overwrite the old Final Exam mark with the new Final Exam (resit) mark. The disadvantage of this is that in Moodle there is no record of the old mark. I can write the old Final Exam score in my diary, but my Head Of Department wants a way whereby the old mark and the new mark are recorded properly in Moodle. What can I do? Kindly advise. Before: Final Exam contributes 50% towards the CFG. Assignment contributes 40% towards the CFG. Test contributes 10% towards the CFG. So in the example above, (18% * 0.5) + (65% * 0.4) + (70% * 0.1) = 42.00. Below 50. A fail grade. Last semester, the student failed because he scored 42/100 which is below the passing mark of 50%. He then took the resit paper and passed. Resit students who pass can only get an overall 50% as the maximum overall mark, which is the CFG. I was not told what the student actually scored in the resit Final Exam. It could have been 20/50 or 29/50. I was not told. I was only told that he passed the resit paper, and that I should edit his Gradebook so that his Course Final Grade (CFG) is a 'C' (a Pass). So what I did was to bump up his Final Exam mark from 9/50 to 17/50 = 34/100. That made his CFG = 50.0 exactly. No more, no less. After: This resulted in him getting an overall score of 50/100. Which is a 'C' grade. (34% * 0.5) + (65% * 0.4) + (70% * 0.1) = 50.00. So that's the quick-and-dirty way I used to get Moodle to show that he scored a 'C' grade for his course. The student does not see the raw Final Exam mark in the Gradebook. Question I So what can I do, I beseech you - O enlightened One - who knows more about Moodle Gradebook than I, to ensure that Moodle can keep a record of BOTH the old Final Exam score and the new Final Exam score? My Head Of Department wants a better more 'scientific' way of entering resit marks without obliterating the old mark. Question II A more complex but proper procedure, that may be necessary in future, is assuming that the ACTUAL resit final exam mark was, let's say, 24/50, and my Head Of Department wanted me to actually record that as 24/50 inside the gradebook, but to have the Course Final Grade to be limited to 50/100 for the resit students. Is there a way to do this complex procedure, O Enlightened One? Indeed, it is my noble Quest to find the answers to these questions. I do hope that I will chance upon an answer from someone more versed with the Moodle Gradebook than I. Regards Frankie Kam A mere Hobbit in Moodle-Shire.

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading By Objectives
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I have just read an article by Ido Millet and Suzanne Weinstein called, "Grading By Objectives: A Matrix Method for Course Assessment." I was wondering if anyone has set up a Moodle gradebook to allow the linking of graded tasks (assignment, exam question, quiz, or project) back to learning objectives?  Is this even possible?  Your file size restrictions here prevent me from attaching the article, however, I was able to attach it in the "General Help" forum. Same question. Same title. For each graded task, the teacher needs to have the ability to specify the relative extent to which the task evaluates each learning objective: either relative weights or points assigned to each task allowing the system to compute the relative grading weight assigned to each learning objective. Also, the article suggests that when a single task generates separate grades for different criteria or subtasks, we should record and treat the grade for each criterion or subtask as a separate assessment with its own weight. Once tasks are graded we can then assess how well students performed on each learning objective.  This will allow teachers to investigate the reasons for poor performance on learning objectives and to change the design of the course to address deficiencies. If we added a way to distinguish between summative and formative activities (or, whether an activity was used for both) it would provide useful information such as the relative assessment attention each learning objective receives in terms of formative assessment, summative assessment or both. Is there a way currently for teachers to: 1) specify learning objectives. 2) allocate each task across these learning objectives. 3) classify each task as summative or formative. If there is not a current way for teachers to do this, what is the process to request that this be made available? Thank you very much! Annie G.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading By Objectives
ResponsesInList.Text: AFAIK , the way in which you use the gradebook is directly related to the way in which you construct your assessment. I am not sure that you would need to make any special change to the gradebook, itself, but discussion is always healthy. You may want to think about how you could ask this question again, only this time in the Gradebook forum , where there can be some serious discussion and consideration of it. An aside: Then I have to ask, "What is new in this idea?" Teachers have long been linking assessment to learning outcomes, or objectives, if you like. A semantic difference is no difference, "a rose by any other name", as someone once wrote. I don't want to argue the article, but I would point out that assessing every proposed objective in individual assessments is just not practicable. The risk would be that it would either take far too much time to make each assessment task or each assessment task would be so superficial that the course could not be assessed adequately or appropriately. This is one of those things that would be nice, but who has the resources or time to make it work as proposed?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading By Objectives
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Colin.  I'll move the question to the Gradebook forum. RE: Aside.  If only teachers were linking assessment to learning outcomes..... "There are three basic methods for constructing a test: topic-based, statistically-based, and objectives-based. Teachers should never use the topic-based approach. [HOWEVER] The topic-based approach is the way in which most tests are created. Almost all teacher education classes have recommended this strategy, and it is probably the only approach commonly used in most classrooms today. Essentially, the instructor takes a given number of questions from Chapter 3 or Topic 1, some number of questions from Chapter 4 or Topic 2, and so on, loosely basing the number of questions on the perceived importance of the topic.  This practice is imprecise and certainly doesn't allow for criterion-referenced interpretation; usually the test score distribution is not widespread enough to allow for norm-referenced interpretation either.  In other words, topic-based construction frequently will not separate test takers as required for norm-referenced tests, nor will it verify specific competencies as does the CRT." Source: 2007. Shrock and Coscarelli. Criterion-referenced test development: technical and legal guidelines for corporate training. 3rd Edition. Finally, if teachers don't take the time to link assessment to learning objectives then they are wasting everyone's time and resources and are assessing nothing (not subject mastery).  It does take time up front, but the effort is worth it because it allows one to accurately assess both student performance and to make improvements to test validity and reliability.

ResponsesInList.Title: SQL Report to show course graded activities and dates
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi everyone!  I am using Moodle 2.9 (upgrading to 3.0 very soon) and am working on putting a report together that shows all graded activities a student has submitted (or not) along with the date it was submitted.  I have created a pretty thorough report but have a problem when retrieving Discussion Forum grades.  I would like to show the last date a forum was posted and haven't a clue how to integrate it into my report.  Any thoughts or suggestions on the below SQL report? 
```text
SELECT 
c.shortname AS "Course Name",
c.ID,
concat( u.firstname, " ", u.lastname ) AS "Student Name",
u.id as "Student ID",
gi.itemmodule AS "Assignment Type",
gi.itemname AS itemname,
gi.grademax AS itemgrademax,
gg.finalgrade AS finalgrade,
DATE_FORMAT(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(gg.timecreated), '+00:00','-04:00'), '%m/%d/%Y %H:%i %p') AS "Time Created",
DATE_FORMAT(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(gg.timemodified), '+00:00','-04:00'), '%m/%d/%Y %H:%i %p') AS "Time Modified"

FROM mdl_course AS c JOIN mdl_context AS ctx ON c.id = ctx.instanceid 
JOIN mdl_role_assignments AS ra ON ra.contextid = ctx.id 
JOIN mdl_user AS u ON u.id = ra.userid AND ra.roleid = 5
JOIN mdl_grade_grades AS gg ON gg.userid = u.id 
JOIN mdl_grade_items AS gi ON gi.id = gg.itemid 
JOIN mdl_grade_categories AS gc ON gi.categoryid=gc.id 
JOIN mdl_course_categories AS cc ON cc.id = c.category

WHERE gi.courseid = c.id
AND c.id = 25333
AND u.deleted <> 1
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Alternative Assignments setup in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: I am looking for help in setting up alternative assignments for a course. For 25% of their grade, students can either take a set of quizzes or write a paper. How would you set this up in the gradebook?  I have given all of my assignments ID #s since that seemed necessary for creating a formula. Thanks for help with this!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternative Assignments setup in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Megan, So there more than one way to accomplish this. Some of it depends on your circumstances/requirements. Here is what I have done in one of my courses: 1. Add your Choice 1 Assignment & first Choice 2 Quiz activity. 2. Then go back and set activity completion for both activities : Assignment: "Student must submit to this activity to complete it." Quiz:  "Student must receive a grade to complete this activity" (if there are no essays). 3. Set up an activity restriction in your first Quiz & Assignment that states if one choice is completed, then the other choice is no longer visible. 4.
Add your remaining 4 Quiz activities. But when you set up a Access
Restriction, add 2 "Restriction Sets." In the first, select 'Completion
tracking' so that the quiz is accessible only when the previous quiz has
been submitted -- repeat with the remaining quizzes. (Or, if you want
all 5 quizzes to be open at the same time, skip this step). For the
second restriction set, add another 'Completion tracking' - choose
Choice Activity 1, but this time change the 'must' into a 'must not' --
Then click the eye ball next to this one only so this will cause these
quizzes to go away once the Assignment is submitted. 6. Grades: The reason to mark the activities to disappear after the other Choice is chosen is so the alternate choices are not visible in the gradebook. In the gradebook, you can set this up a couple ways and it will all depend on 'how' you need your grade book to appear (ie. can you add in a separate category for these activities, or do they need to appear in one of your existing categories; do you need to maintain a specific number as your course total, etc...)... So this part may or may not be useful: But for how we did this, I make the assignment worth the sum of all 5 quizzes, and also make it worth extra credit. This way, if students take the 5 quizzes, they'll get their 25% of the grade with no option to take the extra credit Assignment. If they take the Assignment instead, they will not have access to the Quiz points, but the 25% of the grade will come in the form of the Extra Credit points. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: An SQL query to display the course gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Nadav, try this query 
```text
SELECT


c.id as Course_Id,


c.shortname AS shortname,


c.fullname AS fullname,


u.id AS User_Id,


u.firstname AS firstname, 


u.lastname AS lastname, 


u.email AS email, 


COALESCE(ROUND(gg.finalgrade,2),0) as finalgrade


FROM mdl_user u


INNER JOIN mdl_role_assignments ra ON ra.userid = u.id
```

,gi.itemname, gi.itemtype, gi.itemmodule, gi.iteminstance,gi.grademax, gi.multfactor, gi.plusfactor

JOIN
 mdl_grade_items gi 
ON
 gi.categoryid = gc.id 


WHERE
 gc.courseid = 
XXX

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: An SQL query to display the course gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text:
Updated version: 
```text
SELECT 


gc.courseid, gc.parent, gc.depth, gc.path, gc.fullname "Category",


CASE gc.aggregation


  WHEN 0 THEN 'Mean OF Grades'


  WHEN 2 THEN 'Median OF Grades'


  WHEN 6 THEN 'Highest Grade'


  WHEN 8 THEN 'Mode OF Grades'


  WHEN 10 THEN 'Weighted Mean OF Grades'


  WHEN 11 THEN 'Simple Weighted Mean OF Grades'


  WHEN 12 THEN 'Mean OF Grades (WITH extra credits)'


  WHEN 13 THEN 'SUM OF Grades'


END AS 'aggregation name'


,gi.itemname, gi.itemtype, gi.itemmodule, gi.iteminstance,floor(gi.aggregationcoef2*100) "weight", floor(gi.grademin), floor(gi.grademax), gi.multfactor, gi.plusfactor


FROM mdl_grade_categories gc


JOIN mdl_grade_items gi ON gi.categoryid = gc.id 


WHERE gc.courseid = XXX
```

ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry to wake from the dead an old thread. I had this problem yesterday with a site I was working on and this thread came up on all the searches. It came close but did not contain the specific cause of, or solution to, the problem I had. So in the hope that it might save someone else who has the same problem a few hours, here it is. If your students have the /mod/quiz:preview capability, they will be able to preview quizzes, in the same way a teacher can. But possessing this capability prevents them from "really" attempting quizzes. All attempts will be previews and so not entered in the gradebook. The reason the suggestion elsewhere in this thread to reset the student role's permissions worked, was probably because the student role had inadvertantly been assigned the mod/quiz:preview capability. http://docs.moodle.org/25/en/Capabilities/mod/quiz:preview So if you think this is the case go to: Site Administration->Users->Permissions->Define Roles and click on "Student" in the (default) Manage Roles tab. Type into the filter text box. mod/quiz:preview If it displays and is set to "Allow" then your students quiz attempts will not be entered into the gradebook. That is probably not what you want, so you can click on the edit tab on the same page and uncheck "Allow" Hope it helps someone.

ResponsesInList.Text: We've had a similar situation arise a couple of times: we have an "observer" role which allows the user to view content but not interact.  In a couple of cases, a lecturer has assigned this role to a student to allow them access before their enrolment has officially been processed, and didn't remove it later - so the students did practice attempts instead of real ones. If caught early enough that the preview attempt is still in the database (and you have direct DB access), you can turn it into a "real" attempt easily enough - but preview attempts can be automatically purged for a few reasons, so it needs to be caught early for that to be an option.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades to be rounded down in Moodle 3.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Personally, I'd have expected "round to nearest" to be the standard pretty much everywhere, as that's what's typically meant when speaking about rounding.  Rather than a single issue/decision, I'd suggest that this is really the interplay of two issues: Lack of clarity in the "decimal places" setting(s) - is it rounding or truncating? Order of operations - are letter grades calculated before or after the rounding (or truncation)? Simply changing the rounding/truncation strategy still seems to leave room for confusion, as letter grade boundaries can themselves contain decimal places (which may not have been the case when MDL-21746 was first opened, based on the early comments).  Consider the following scenario: The lower boundary for an A is 89.5% Student 1 scores 89.4% Student 2 scores 89.6% If we simply round down (truncate) to 0 decimal places, both will see a score of 89%, but Student 1 gets a B while Student 2 gets an A. Perhaps we should add a new "letter grade strategy" setting (subject to better naming), with options such as: Round, then apply letter grade Round, but apply letter grade to raw score Truncate, then apply letter grade Truncate, but apply letter grade to raw score As I understand it, the second option is the current Moodle behaviour, so should probably be the default (so that there are no unexpected changes upon upgrade). There's also the completely non-technical solution: rather than actually changing how it works, simply make the current behaviour clearer by flagging grades which have been rounded to/over letter grade boundaries in some way.  This could either mean flagging them to teachers, so that they can choose to either adjust the affected grades as desired, or flagging them to everyone who can see the grade in question (so that students can also see that their grade was just below the boundary).  Flagging to students needn't reveal the raw grade (though it probably should for teachers, so they can see just how close the student came) - simply pointing out that the displayed grade has been rounded up should hopefully make it clear why there's a discrepancy, though.  This could even be combined with the technical solution, so that if a "letter grade strategy" which applies the letters based on raw grade is chosen, there's still an indication as to why there's a discrepancy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CLAMP LAEgrader Report with Frozen Headers and Names
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, Yes, in fact its recommended that you hide the regular Grader report (though it cannot be hidden from the site admin). The steps: Site Administration block->Users->Permissions->Define Roles With each role (likely only editingteacher and teacher, unless you've cloned some) edit the role change the gradereport/grader:view capabilities to "prohibit" Save the permission changes As mentioned, the admin will always see both reports. There is one caveat to the above mentioned exercise... hardcoding outside the plugin branches causes the default grade report to search: first for the last report the user used then for a report called "grader" if present and accessible for this role then for a report called "user" if present, blah, blah, blah then alphabetically Because of this, unless you also happen to have the laeuser, the first time a teacher uses the gradebook they will get the user report. If you had the laeuser report you'd have depermissioned the User report (similar to above) and the alphabetical search would set the laegrader report as the default. The laeuser report is in limited distribution and planned for general distribution within the next four weeks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 回复: CLAMP LAEgrader Report with Frozen Headers and Names
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Min, I'm guessing your course total is set to display type, "Real" which in our gradebook means "points".  Point calculations will never take into account weights, nor can they -- they are just a tallying of the total points.  Percentage grades and letter grades take into account weights so if you used a display type of "percent" or "letter" for you course total, you should see your weights accurately reflected.  If the maximums for both quizzes are 100 and 10, respectively than your course total would show 100% or A (in English). To change the display type of the course total, turn editing on and click the edit icon (usually a hand with a pencil) under the course total header.

ResponsesInList.Text: SELECT u.username, gg.finalgrade FROM mdl_grade_grades gg JOIN mdl_grade_items gi on gg.itemid = gi.id JOIN mdl_course c on c.id = gi.courseid JOIN mdl_user u on u.id = gg.userid WHERE c.id = <your course id> AND u.id = <your user id> AND gi.itemtype = 'course'

ResponsesInList.Text: We have only seen this when certain PHP ini values are set too low or not set at all (approximating the same thing). If you're using PHP 5.3.9 you need a line like php_value max_input_vars XXXXX where XXXXX is a similar calculation as above with suhosin.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all, We have 2  final quizzes in which  one of them is the main quiz  and 2nd quiz is for students who want to improve their grades or were not attending the 1st quiz. In such case, we wish to calculate the only latest grade that a student got. For example , if a student submitted 2 quizzes, so only the second quiz will be calculated in the gradebook. However if the student submit only the  the 2nd quiz, then only this grade will be calculated. I will appreciate any help, Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Miki, You could create a subcategory and change the category total to a custom calculation that looks at the second, and takes that score unless it's empty. Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, I have exactly the same problem as Miki, but I am not sure which exam I should take into a subcategory. I have a main grade category which wears the name of the course and I use natural aggregation in it. I have two subcategories such as exams and homeworks. The exams subcategory involves two items, the main exam and the second exam. So my question is which item ( exam and/or the second exam ) I should take into a new subcategory? Should I use a custom calculation in exams subcategrory which is directed to the second exam item? In this case, does the moodle take only into account the second exam item if the point is filled out? Thank you in advance for your answer. Best regards, Zoltán

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Both exams should go in the subcategory and then the calculation should be written at the category level. Something to the effect of If Exam B is not null, Exam B total ...else Exam A total (that is not correctly formatted - just entered to give you an idea)

ResponsesInList.Title: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Emma, Thank you for your answer, but I do not know how I could write such a formul, since there is no if-else logical structure in the custom calculation. My category structure is the following: category named 'Exames' [subcategory named '1.exam' [ item named 'MainExam' (ID: Ex1), item named 'SecondExam' (ID: Ex2), ] ] The subcategory total is calculated by natural aggregation, while the category total is calculated by custom calculation with the following formula: '=[[Ex2] ]' (the space between ] ] is intentional here.) However this solution is not working correctly. Could you tell me where is the fault? Best regards, Zoltán

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Because your calculation is telling the category to use the value of exam 2 for the total, regardless of whether there is a value in there or not. You might look at this post - I think maybe it could help to achieve what you are looking for. https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=171508

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Or you might use the max argument.  That would pull the higher of the two scores - would that not achieve the result you are looking for?

ResponsesInList.Title: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you again your answer. I have written the following custom formula which works correctly as Miki wrote: = floor( (Ex2+1)/(Ex2+1)*Ex2 + Ex1*(1-Ex2/(Ex2+0.01))) Best regards, Zoltán

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: How to calculate late exam in the gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Glad you were able to figure it out and thanks for sharing the answer.

Any thoughts on what I might be missing? Thanks in advance. -Joe

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV import error: "One of the grade values is larger than the allowed grade maximum of 100"
ResponsesInList.Text: Joe, Make sure the Admin setting " Grade point maximum" / gradepointmax is >= the largest assignment at your school. It defaults to 100. Also if you create a grade item through import it defaults to 100, so creating it first with a point total of 150 and/or allowing " Unlimited grades" / unlimitedgrades. Though you will still need to change the max grade to 150 for that item afterwards if you create it through an import.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV import error: "One of the grade values is larger than the allowed grade maximum of 100"
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a setting in Moodle 2.8 and above. You can change the max number of points allowed in activities . Site admin > Grades > General settings > Grade point maximum. The other setting to check is Site admin > Grades > General settings > Unlimited grades to allow point values that are over 100% for a given item. Remember also that when you import into a new grade item, it will default to being 100 points (or whatever you have set in Grade point default). If you're importing an item that is not worth whatever you have set there, best practice is to create the grade item first as otherwise you'll have to change the number of points the item is worth after the fact.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV import error: "One of the grade values is larger than the allowed grade maximum of 100"
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm updating this in case anyone runs into this issue. Site admin > Grades > General settings > Grade point maximum. The other setting to check is Site admin > Grades > General settings > Unlimited grades to allow point values that are over 100% for a given item.
