ResponsesInList.Title: Why only 100 points for "Grade"?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry if this suggestion has been posted before! One feature in Gradebook that seems to cause me to jump through hoops when setting up courses, is the "Grade" pick box I get when I'm setting up an activity. It seems that the assumption being made is that all assignments are graded on a percentage basis. At least that's the only reason I can think of to explain why you can only award 100 points. However, my courses are set up so that each assignment, quiz, test etc. earns a student a particular number of points. But if an assignment is worth 130 points, I have to jump through hoops to convert it into 100 percentage points and make sure it is weighted appropriately. It would be much simpler and easier to be able to type in 120 points (i.e., kill the pick box altogether). In Categories and Items, I could then compute a simple average for the final grade. In fact, the same can be said for collections of assignments (average of quizzes, average of week one grades etc.). No muss, no fuss. Thanks for all the hard work going in to Moodle! Cheers! Devin

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why only 100 points for "Grade"?
ResponsesInList.Text: Devin: For historical reasons, Moodle used a drop-down menu for entering grades.  This was always a positive integer, and had a maximum value of 100, although each module lets you set it to a lower value. You can enter grades directly into the gradebook with the latest version of Moodle, and those can exceed 100 points, and you can enter decimals.  Of course, you can display those as the entered values, as percentages, or as letter grades. Within the modules, you can also patch the code to have values greater than 100.  I have shown how to do that in this tutorial on patching forms: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Patching_forms_tutorial Some have gone even further (we have at our school), that lets you enter decimal grade in the modules, but that requires making changes to the database , etc. so you should try to make sure that the above does what you want before taking any further steps. --Gary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why only 100 points for "Grade"?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: =sum of grades

ResponsesInList.Title: Suggested gradebook improvements (was Wanted: User testing of Moodle 1.9.5 gradebook improvements)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, Here is our list. Sorry, it’s rather long . Most of it repeats what one can see above in this thread; plus some of the items are already listed for Stage 2 . 1. Bulk grade exception interface - we had it in 1.8, so it would be really nice to have it back ( MDL-13889 ). 2. Ability to flood-fill same grades for groups or for the whole class ( MDL-18010 ). A number of faculty have group work, thus they often want to provide the same grade for a group of students. 3. Make sure that hidden assignment equals hidden grade right away, since at the moment one has to remember to hide the grade separately in the gradebook ( MDL-16381 ) 4. Align Instructor and Student view for hidden items (aka add an option to aggregate only non-hidden items MDL-11837 ). At the moment Instructors see hidden items, which are included into the total in Grader and User reports. Students do not see hidden items, and for them those items are not included into the total for User report. Thus, the grade displayed is drastically different. It seems that a lot of users are thinking that gradebook calculations are incorrect because of such discrepancy in views. 1.8 had that option already, since instructors were able to set Show Hidden Items to No, which successfully removed all hidden items from their view and calculations.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suggested gradebook improvements (was Wanted: User testing of Moodle 1.9.5 gradebook improvements)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your suggestions, Elena. 1. Sure, that's already in the list. 2. We'll need a tracker issue and votes for this. I'm not sure it would be widely used. 3. You will have to wait for Moodle 2.0 for this. It requires complete centralisation of all grading/feedback into the gradebook. Currently, because each module has its own grading code, this is not possible in 1.9 4. This is an important point which should be fixed in stage 2. It requires a new category setting: "Aggregate hidden items", which would be on by default to retain backward compatibility. 5. Already in stage 2 list 6. Already in stage 2 list 7.a) Need to wait for 2.0, for same reasons as 3) 7.b) You can rename the course category to anything you want. The shortname can sometimes be rather cryptic, so I'm not sure it would be much good as a default either. 8. Originally we had many settings to control the look of the grader report. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suggested gradebook improvements (was Wanted: User testing of Moodle 1.9.5 gradebook improvements)
ResponsesInList.Text: Nicolas, Mary's issue stems from the extra credit in the parent categories being applied two different ways. The first way is correct, where an extra credit grade DOES NOT increase the maximum category total for the parent. The parent category total is based solely off the non extra credit category and the extra credit points are added to the student's parent category total, not the parent's category total maximum grade. This example would NOT hurt the student if they chose not to participate in the extra credit assignments. The second way is incorrect. An extra credit child element should NEVER increase the parent's category total, only the grade someone receives. The parent category here is based of the sum of BOTH the non extra credit category and the extra credit category. This example would greatly hurt a student who did not participate in the extra credit assignments. A good example is this: If a child receives and extra credit grade of 5/50 points for an extra credit category of grades and receives 95/100 points in a sibling non-extra credit category. The student's grade should be calculated as 95+5/100 for 100% NOT 95+5/150 for 66.67%, as extra credit would then be severely hurting the student instead of helping them. Extra credit should NEVER decrease a student's grade in ANY aggregation method. Neither should drop-lowest and keep-highest. That said, unless we can see Mary's grade-book, there may be something else going on that is not coming across in the forum. I am simply responding to this: 6. This doesn't look incorrect to me. You've set the category as extra credit in both cases, so it's perfectly normal that it affects the parent category's total in both cases. Your course category is also set to Sum of Grades, so once again it is normal that the extra credit affects it. Please help me understand your statement above. As I understand extra credit as it is used at a major University, it should never affect the maximum possible grade for a category total and it should ALWAYS help someone who participates in an extra credit assignment. This fundamental nature of extra credit could potentially lead to grades and percentages above the maximum, this is why so many who use extra credit were clamoring for grades and percentages above the maximum, as in the above good example, it is entirely possible for a student to get 150/100 or 150% in the parent category.

In 1.9 you may add columns directly to the gradebook, but you still will not have an option to give 4 numeric grades for one assignment. You can try to play with scales and outcomes. Scales should be included in the aggregation for the whole installation by an admin. Then an instructor should - create a scale to be used later - set up 4 outcomes with that scale - create an offline assignment and apply all 4 outcomes to it Take a look at this documentation: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Scales http://docs.moodle.org/en/Outcomes

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook 1.9 Problem - I Need Inline Feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, Thanks for the very clear screenshots. The problem is that your student's grade was overridden in the gradebook. This locks the grading mechanisms of the linked activity (in this case, assignment) for this particular grade, to prevent your change from being overridden by the activity. You probably changed this grade by mistake. What you can do, in the gradebook view, is turn editing on, then edit the grade (click the hand-and-pencil icon next to the grade), and untick the "Overridden" checkbox. The original grade will appear, and you will be able to provide feedback through the assignment interface again.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add external grades
ResponsesInList.Text: I can't help with the moodle side, but in your excel formula the average functions aren't actually doing anything and are unnecessary. AVERAGE() returns the average of multiple numbers, so if you entered AVERAGE(A1:A10) the result would be the average of cells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and A10. You are only passing the function a single number and the average of a single number is the same as the number. So in fact your formula only needs to be: =A1*10/100+B1*10/100+C1*40/100+D1*40/100 or: =A1*0.1+B1*0.1+C1*0.4+D1*0.4 (which is the same thing, just less typing) Maybe try this in moodle and see how you go.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebookplus version 2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eduardo, It sounds like you are experiencing two issues. The quizes and assignments don't allow for decimal grades by default. The hack to adjust this is relatively simple, if you modify the table structure to store decimal grades, then gradebook plus will allow you to edit grades as decimals. Then you can ensure that all of your quizzes and assignments are set as 7 points max, I think you will see two decimal places though. Concerning weighting and reporting via the gradebook; it is based off of 100. However, I think you can get something close to the reporting you want without having to change any code. Setting every category to weight of 7 "weight" for the category on a 0-7 scale you can then aggregate these column totals as you see fit. You will get a warning on the set weights screen that "the total weights is not equal to 100", ignore this warning and see if the calculations are what you are looking for. The calculations are assuming 1-100 scale so behavior may be a bit erratic. I think what will happen is the "weighted contribution column" will have correct values of points for the categories, but the total will reported as a percent (of 100). So you will have to multiply your final weighted percent by 7 to obtain what you want. Also change the advanced preferences to "show weighted grades" and probably don't display points or raw percent. Additionally you could adjust the "grade letters" to report what you want. So you would create a grade letter system that maps 0-100 numbers to a 0.0-7.0 scale. So roughly every 1.43 points on the 1-100 scale maps to 0.1 points on your 0.0-7.0 scale. All of this really just points out the need for a centralised, extensible pluggable gradebook system. If you have funds, Martin D. is looking to gather funds to make this happen via moodle.com. hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading Strategy Help Needed!

ResponsesInList.Title: Community input requested on some  Gradebook 1.9 terms
ResponsesInList.Text: Nicolas and Helen asked to get community feedback on revising some of the terminology for improving usability in gradebook in 1.9 an beyond. For background, many of the terms seemed to be sensible to the developers, but they were not intuitive to teacher in the field. Hence, special training has been required and remembering the meanings from term to term is also a problem. Here are my suggestions and an attached page from the gradebook configuration page (Categories and items) with my suggested improvements Aggregation -> Summarize by (Aggregation is a pretty technical term not used in grading) Weighted mean of grades -> Weighted grades (Simplifies the term and people don't think of this as taking a mean) Mean of grades -> Average of percentages (This method converts grade items to percentages and averages them. This term is more intuitive) Simple weighted mean of grades -> Average of points (This common method totals points earned and divides by points possible. Mean of grades (with extra credit) -> Eliminate and implement extra credit in a standard way Mode of grades -> Eliminate or comment out in the source code to simplify Multipliplicator -> Multiple grade by (The original term is too technical an not intuitive) Offset -> Add to grade (The original term is too technical an not intuitive) Please comment on whether you agree that these terms would improve usability, if you have other suggestions, an if you think he change is worth it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Community input requested on some  Gradebook 1.9 terms
ResponsesInList.Text: Elena: Thanks for moving this along and your other suggestions for simplifying the gradebook. A few notes: 1. What is currently called Sum of grades and Simple weighted mean of grades (average of points) are almost identical. In both cases, activities with more points contribute more than those with fewer. The second method has the benefit that, by default, items not yet graded are not factored into the total. Hence a student can determine, based on what has been graded, that they currently have a B+, etc. 2. I agree that Multiplicator, the ability to set category values (instead of having them computed from the items in them), and a separate weight field is very confusing. All seem to allow scores to be scaled in a very similar way. I think that weight does this best, and Multiplicator, if the name is changed and kept as advanced, does not do much harm. I have suggested to Nicolas that he not have category values be an editable field in the category and items setting page to help avoid confusion. 3. While I agree with you that Mean of grades seems to be the "average of points", but that is not how it is computed. Values are converted to percents first so that every item has equal weight. The phrase "Average of percentages" best describes what a teacher would be thinking if they did it manually. See strategry 2 in http://docs.moodle.org/en/Gradebook_1.9_Tutorial . Thanks for your input and thoughts. Based on this and other comments received in this discussion I will ty to come up with a revised list in a few days that addresses the various observations. --Gary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Community input requested on some  Gradebook 1.9 terms
ResponsesInList.Text: I think many of the suggestions have merit. However, I would prefer to make changes via the language editing page on our sites, rather than having the common confusion of re-learning the phrasings discussions here at the Moodle site. For example, we'd often be saying, "I have x suggestion about the presentation of the Calculation Method (formerly Aggregation) and the Course Grades (formerly Grader Report)...etc." After carefully reviewing the terminology being suggested, I vote conservatively to avoid changing most of these terms now that they have been introduced as defaults. In the exceptions noted below, I favor re-phrasings that add to the original. Other thoughts/votes: Grades > Points We need to avoid saying points and stick with "grades" as common nomenclature for American English en_us (and "marks" for other English speaking groups). IMHO , points can have too many meanings. Aggregate > Summarize Summarize is too similar to "sum" and would be objectionable to our Math faculty. I think most graders will be able to understand aggregation. Aggregation Method > Calculation Method Keep the same words used now and add the word Method. A calculation is a method and there are other functions that allow the user to set a calculation method. Saying Aggregation Calculation is also descriptive and yet awkward. With new gradebook 1.9 users I am finding that they need to distinguish settings that affect the calculation/method of aggregating vs. settings that affect the display of the aggregation result. Aggregation Method could replace Aggregation on the category editing page (grade/edit/tree/category.php) without increasing confusion. On the Grader Report page (grade/report/grader/index.php): My report preferences (tab) > My report display Preferences On Category editing page (grade/edit/tree/category.php): My report preferences > My category display preferences And I agree and vote for the idea of changing the drop down menu item below: Course Settings > Gradebook Settings (or Course Gradebook Settings) Yes to all of these: Add X to grade, Multiply grade by X, Drop X Lowest Grades, Keep X Highest Grades. These are all improvements in the same approach, they clarify by adding to the existing default phrasing. - Kathy C Brandeis University

ResponsesInList.Title: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: In response to Helen's request for input on new features, I would like to make a case for an option to include extra credit assignments that allow student's course or category totals to exceed 100%.  Basically, this is an extra credit assignment where any points earned are added to the student’s total points earned for the course or category, but the total possible points in the course or category is not increased. This is not currently a feature in Moodle. In my experience, this type of extra credit is very common in American secondary and post-secondary education and is a high priority for our faculty. If you would also like to be able to include extra credit assignments of this type, please vote for this issue in the tracker: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-12380 For many of us who are in environments where this type of extra credit is widely used this is an essential feature. In my search for a solution to this I have seen quite a few similar posts on “how do I do extra credit?” I think because this concept is so pervasive in our environment, many users assume that there is already a way to accomplish this and that they just haven’t figured out how to use it. However, it isn’t currently a feature at all. Additionally, I suspect that many of us in environments where extra credit needs to be used would like to see such a feature compatible with the "simple weighted mean of grades" aggregation strategy so that instructors would have the ability to use extra credit AND show students an accurate "running total" through the "aggregate only non-empty grades" option. Some discussion on this has already taken place here: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-12942

ResponsesInList.Title: Extra credit: what is the underlying mathematical structure?
ResponsesInList.Text: Every time the Extra Credit thing comes up, the mathematician in me wants to know what is really going on. However, I have not yet made the time to sit down and try to work it out. Actually, I am not even sure I know mathematical structure that ordinary grades from. You might define: A grade G is a pair of numbers $$(g, g_{max}) \in \mathbb{R}^2$$ with $$0 \le g \le g_{max}$$ . And then you can rigorously define various operations like add, scale, ... on them in a fairly natural way. Or would it work out more neatly with the definition A grade G is a pair of numbers $$(p, g_{max}) \in \mathbb{R}^2$$ with $$0 \le p \le 1$$ and $$0 \le g_{max}$$ . (That is, work more directly with the percentage grade. The two are virtually equivalent, you would probably need to try both to decide which was nicer.) Anyway, neither of these definitions lead to a Vector space, Ring or other algebraic structure I remember from my maths degree.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: "I've never understood how you can get more than 100% (or equally get 100% even though you got some of the questions wrong). Is this just some silly way to make people feel better that they got a high % rather than just saying that a lower % is a good mark?" If I make a curve set from less than the class high score, then the outliers at the top will have more than 100%. For example, if the high score is 99, but the rest of the As are clustered around 92, then I might curve down from 92, treating 92 as a perfect score. My outlier student at 99 would then have a result higher than 100%. The rationale for this approach is that I do not assume that my teaching or assessment is perfect. If students cannot score 100%, it might be because I presented it imperfectly, or because my assessment does not accurately measure their grasp of the material. To deal with this problem, I assume that the best students are reflecting my best teaching and assessment, and curve down from them. However, sometimes you have an outlier who outperforms everyone else in the class significantly. Sometimes, I assume this is random, and disregard that score when setting the curve.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: Basically, the extra credit assignment is an optional assignment where the numerator (points earned) is added to the course total of points earned, but the denominator (points possible) is not added to the course total points possible. This allows an instructor to give students the option to do extra work by completing the extra credit assignment to make up for poor performance in other assignments, but does not penalize students who choose not to complete the optional extra credit assignment. Here is an example of possible outcomes from three different students in the same course: There are four 25 point assignments and one 5 point extra credit assignment. Student A: A1: 24/25 + A2: 23/25 + A3: 20/25 + A4: 22/25 + Extra Credit: 5 (student completed extra credit assignment) = 94/100 Student B: A1: 21/25 + A 2: 23/25 + A3: 22/25 + A 4: 19/25 + Extra Credit: 0 (student did not attempt extra credit) = 85/100 Student C: A1: 23/25 + A2: 25/25 + A3: 24/25 + A4: 24/25 + Extra Credit: 5 (student completed extra credit assignment) = 101/100 The case of Student C, where a student has done well on all assignments and completes extra credit, earning a course total score above 100% is a relatively rare, but it does occur. I know it must seem strange if you’ve never seen the concept before. It is a pretty standard element in American secondary and post-secondary education.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: We had exactly the same logical argument with our faculty...and we lost. Apparently, the big issues are motivation, and class ranking, and inspiring greater competition. If you have a few students at the top of a very competitive class, instructors want the option of having grades go over the max. When we implemented these changes, student support questions about their grades drastically dropped. So the occurence is not as rare as we would like to believe. The biggest argument however, was that if we implemented the feature, and it didn't come in to play, no one would notice or care. But if we didn't, and it was needed, there would be support calls about it. Compared with our statistical data detailing the number of support calls about "my grade is capped at 100", it was obvios that they were correct.

You could even hack the grader and user reports so that the Real display of grades are appended with a % symbol. This would certainly give the impression of having grades over the maximum. Compared with the nightmare involved with implementing, aggregating and maintaining grades over 100%, I really think this compromise is more than acceptable.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: But unless you allow grades to to over the maximum, aggregation will be incorrect. The way it boiled down was this: there were a handful of us who believed percents above 100 did not make sense, and a committee representing our 1900 faculty who wanted grades above max and percents above 100 to happen. The feature being there does not affect those who do not take advantage of it, but if it were missing, those who would make use of it are out of luck. Mathematically, 100% is all, everything, the whole shebang. But even some of our mathematics instructors wanted this feature. I agree that using calculations and some report hacks, you can simulate grades over 100%, but less (far less) than 1% of our faculty correctly coaxed calculations to calculate anything remotely close to reality. So instead of asking all of our faculty to change their way of thinking and working, we adapted Moodle to fit their needs. Having these features (grades above max and percents above 100) in Moodle make it unique and special among other learning management systems. BTW , great discussion. It's very hard for me to argue with you as I believe exactly as you do, but ultimately this is a tool to ease teaching and learning. Therefore the faculty and students won out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: Our gradebook ( http://cvs.moodle.org/contrib/patches/LSU_gradebook/ ) allows for grades above the maximum grade (up to 2X), grades above the 100% (up to 200%), assignment grades up to 500pts, and extra credit in SUM, Weighted Mean, and Simple Weighted Mean. Weighted mean Each grade item can be given a weight, which is then used in the arithmetic mean aggregation to influence the importance of each item in the overall mean. Each grade within a category (or a category total within a parent) is normalized to a decimal value based on the quotient between the points earned and the maximum ensuring that weights are calculated appropriately. Grades up to 2X the maximum can be entered resulting in grades up to 200%. Extra credit grade items are tacked on after category calculation has taken place. A1 70/100 weight 10, A2 20/80 weight 5, A3 10/10 weight 3, category max 100, and one extra credit item worth 5/10: (0.7*10 + 0.25*5 + 1.0*3)/18 = (0.625)*100 --> 62.5 + 5 = 67.5pts OR 67.5% Simple weighted mean The difference from Weighted mean is that weight is calculated as Maximum grade - Minimum grade for each item. 100 point assignment has weight 100, 10 point assignment has weight 10. Grades up to 2X the maximum can be entered resulting in grades up to 200%. This is the mean that most instructors are used to. A1 70/100, A2 20/80, A3 10/10, category max 100, and one extra credit item worth 5/10: (0.7*100 + 0.25*80 + 1.0*10)/190 = (0.526*100) --> 52.6 + 5 = 57.6pts OR 57.6% Sum of grades The sum of all grade values. Scale grades are ignored. This is the only type that does not convert the grades to percentages internally (normalization). The Maximum grade of associated category item is calculated automatically as a sum of maximums from all aggregated items. Grades up to 2X the maximum can be entered resulting in grades up to 200%. Keep highest and drop lowest values are not calculated using this aggregation method for obvious reasons. A1 70/100, A2 20/80, A3 10/10, and one extra credit item worth 5/10: 70 + 20 + 10 = 100 + 5 --> 105pts OR (105/190) = 55.3% Please be aware that extra credit is added to the REAL point total of it's given category after all other calculations have taken place. The conversion to percentages happens AFTER extra credit has been added. Extra credit is NOT normalized in any way, simply added to the category point total and before percentages are calculated. Sorry if my maths skills aren't up to Tim's.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New feature discussion: Extra credit and course total scores above 100%
ResponsesInList.Text: 1/ How to deal with letter grades and scales when using >100% grades? How are we going to visualise it in gradebook reports? Letter grades are based on the minimum necessary to achieve a grade, therefore, if a 92% is the minimum necessary for an A, then 122% is above that and qualifies for an A. This is how it works in our system. 2/ What is the real "correct" maximum for >100% grades - is it 200% or 300% or 110%, this value is important because it affects the total grade in some cases We set ours at a hardcoded multiplier of 2X, so 200% and double the maximum. This could trivially become an administrator (less trivially for courses) preference (setting to 1 disables overgrading). 3/ How are we going to tell if teacher entered incorrect value or just wanted to give >100% How do we know they weren't one person off when entering grades? You can't check for carelessness. 4/ How to deal with letter/scale grades >100% in gradebook exports and imports? All grades function as they normally do, except now you have the ability to go over the maximum, and therefore 100%. Exports of grades above the max and 100% function as they should. Imports of grades above the max and above 100% behave as they should as well. We have already solved these issues in our current implementation and have released the code on Moodle's CVS . We have been using this on a large scale installation (30,000 students and 1900 faculty with over 13,000 unique logins per day) for almost a year. We have some upgrade problems to iron out as well as some more simplification to do. 5/ Does it make sense to support <0% grades? Makes absolutely NO sense to me, but some faculty want this.

ResponsesInList.Title: What is the best way to backup your grade book?
ResponsesInList.Text: We had a bit of Moodle meltdown last week, I guess it was not too bad given it only effected 3 out of 800 users but it sent alarm bells a ringin. Three students had a strange issue where when they logged into moodle they appeared as one of the other students. It was a trianglar thing. Kellie would log in and she came up as Betty, Betty would log in and she came up as Prue and Prue would log in an she came up as Kellie. Weird!!!!! Anyway, in a silly attemp to rectify the problem we deleted Betty, Prue and Keillie and then recreated them. Not a good plan. They came back just fine but we lost all there assement info for the whole semester. OOOOOps. Anyway we are working on getting that back but ....... How do individual teachers back up their gradebooks? Do they have to backup the whole course with user data or is there a quicker way? Can we automate this process to avoid me having Betties mum on the phone complaining that her daughter is in tears because her work is lost. We have 30 teachers with 6 weeks of assessment info in the gradebook. What is the best way to back that up?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the best way to backup your grade book?
ResponsesInList.Text: Rob: You can export the gradebook an excel and other types of files, but as a practical matter, it is something most of us would not do often enough. You can automate backing up courses, but that has its problems too, especially for large sites. What probably is a good idea is to backup your database once or twice a day and send it to another machine that is very separate from the main server (like offsite, etc.) Given today's hard drive costs, the space needed is almost trivial. Backing up the data folders for uploaded files should probably be done on a regular basis also. For our own school, with 500 students and three years of work and all work preserved, the database size is 1GB and the data size is 15GB, uncompressed. The database, in particular, compresses really well. If you were able to restore the database to a test machine that was before this data was lost, you could at least get the grading information back for this type of case (and the same thing could be used for security issues, etc.) So, I would suggest that this is a wake up call to automate the process. One other thing for students to keep in mind: even though the detailed recording of the learning was lost, the learning still happened. I suspect that an arrangement can be worked out between the teacher and student as to how the final grade will be determined that would satisfy everyone. --Gary

If we republish the SCORM package with an option to report all interactions (v/s page completion and overall score only) the grades are passed instantly when the students are completing the SCORM. That is good, but generates large amount of useless data - the trainers really don't want to have all interactions reported - just the overall scores and slide completion. Our Authorware generated SCORMS would not pass data to the Gradebook. If we re-save the coresponding item in the Gradebook - just as with Captivate, all SCORM scores received by students until this update is made, are passed successfully, but will not be passed when the students are completing the SCORM. Due to the fact that we have numerous Authorware and Captivate SCORMs we desparately need to figure out what is the solution. Any ideas and help will be greatly appreciated.

Now I'm trying to use it effectively, which is hard! I have bulk loaded a whole school year group. These students do a variety of subjects (not on Moodle - just in school). I want teachers to select a student, upload an example of work for that student in a particular subject e.g. Art, and assign a grade to that work. Each student will have an example of graded work for each subject they study. I don't know if Moodle is good for this. At this stage I'm not creating a course for students to enrol on, just a library of graded work examples per student per department. Has anyone done something similar? What would be a good strategy for me to take? I'd appreciate ideas to help me progress with this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: building a library of graded work
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, 1) " upload an example of work for that student" Will it be work sample that was created by that student, or some outside sample? 2) "and assign a grade to that work" Will it be a grade for a student or for work sample that was done by someone else? 3) Should students be able to see each other samples or grades? Or is it for Instructor access/review only? I guess I am confused why it would be teachers who would load work samples, and not students themselves

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: building a library of graded work
ResponsesInList.Text: Good questions! 1) These would all be samples created by the student, but selected by the teacher. 2) It would be a grade for the particular piece of student work - the work selected by the teacher in (1). Some of this work is in hard copy and the teacher will need to scan or digitise it. 3) Excellent question - the idea is that it is for instructor access/review BUT it would certainly be very good to create a sample library of graded work for students to browse to get a clearer understanding of quality and associated grade. Why teachers not students? Moodle isn't used in my school (at present). I want to create a system that does the above as a means for teachers to track and assign grades to student samples for outside agencies to view when required and to help standardisation within departments. But, I've heard lots of good things about Moodle and thought this was an excellent opportunity to get to grips with it. Once I do, I can start to experiment with it in my classes and role it out slowly. I've created my own simple systems that allow students to upload files for me to access - but Moodle is on a whole other scale of operation! I'm trying to find out how well I can customise it to serve different requirements - this is my first task. I appreciate your interest.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: building a library of graded work
ResponsesInList.Text: From what I hear you do not really need to load students (create user accounts for students in Moodle), since you just want to create public browseable repository of student work. In fact, probably it would be better not to associate a sample with a particular student for privacy reasons. Moodle has various activities and tools, and in your particular situation I would try to use either of those: - Forums (create bunch of forums like in this course, name them: Art samples, History samples, etc. Decide whether Standard or Single Simple forum would look better in your case. Instructors would simply post there, attach student work to the posts and state what grade had been given and why). I like forums since they are easy, searchable, and have email subscriptions. - Glossaries (Similar to forums, but you may introduce categories and keywords) - Databases (thisone is a little tricky for a new user to set up, but at the end it will be almost exactly what you want - public repository of entries with potential comments. Like in here ) Since you are new, I would recommend to see all those tools in action here , and read some documentation while trying to build mockups. (to moderators: I would probably transfer this thread to General forum or Teaching tips and tricks )

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the guidance Elena. You're right, I don't need student accounts but a repository accessible to other designated individuals. I'll spend some time researching your suggestions and if/when I get stuck I'll post to the General forum (which I hope you contribute to as well). But I'm wondering whether it will be easier just to set something up of my own; a few drop down menus and an upload button! Once more, thanks for your input, I'm very grateful for it. pgeo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: building a library of graded work
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, An interesting case. It depends on what you're trying to achieve. If you want to ensure common moderation across staff within a faculty then you could set up a module within a course than only teachers could see (i.e. just hide it). Alternatively, agreeing in some part with Elena, you could try using a Wiki-style repository. If you use Moodle then you could set up the graded piece of work as an offline assignment. Then, staff can put their grades/thoughts on the piece and compare notes afterwards. I use this with my students whereby each student uploads a piece of work and everyone else grades it (with comments/reasons) and I comment on the entire effort and upload that for them to see. This turns all my students into markers (how can they reach a standard if they can't recognise it?). Alternatively, if you want to show standards (to students or staff) then just upload the example with comments. For each task my students see the current requirements and then they can go to a similar (i.e. last year's) task, see what was written, view the feedback those students were given, and then see examples of the best work (suitably anonymised). Hope this helps. Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can gradebook export Username field?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can gradebook export Username field?
ResponsesInList.Text: On line 259 of grade/export/lib.php change email to username as so: echo "$user->firstname$user->lastname$user->idnumber$user->institution$user->department$user->e mail"; becomes echo "$user->firstname$user->lastname$user->idnumber$user->institution$user->department$user->username"; You can then use the language string editor to change the email string to username.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting grade letter site-level defaults problem
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are not using grades, you do not need to touch the grade letters. They are only used for display purposes anyway, so if you hide the gradebook from your students, they will never see any grades. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Column averages in Grader reports
ResponsesInList.Text: No there isn't. There are two related reasons for that: 1. The figures in the row of column averages are calculated on-the-fly, they are not stored in the database . 2. If we included these figures in the exports, the data could no longer be used in imports because of this extra row of data If you want to use the exports for reasons other than imports, you can use a simple AVG() excel formula on each column, or copy-paste the row of averages from the grader report.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I keep attendance out of the gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two solutions here: put the attendance grade item in a category with grade type set to "None", then hide the category so users cannot see it. change a few lines of code in the attendance module to prevent it from registering with the gradebook. Let's start with the first method, since it involves no hacks. Whenever I use activity name , replace it with the name you gave to your new attendance activity. When you create a new attendance activity in your course, at the bottom of the form you can choose the grade category. It defaults to "uncategorised". Select instead "New category". Save your attendance activity Go to Grades -> grader report You will see your attendance activity inside a category called " activity name " Next to the " activity name " grade item is another called "Category total". If not already done, click the button "Turn editing on" A little edit icon appears beneath the Category Total heading Click this icon In the "Grade type" drop-down menu, select "None" Save your changes Hide the activity name category (there should be a little "eye" icon under the heading, if not click the " Hide show/hide icons" link above the report, it should make the icon appear). This will hide the whole category from students in your course. Now for the second solution: You need to comment out a few lines in two files: In attendances.php, comment out lines 76 and 85 (put // at the beginning) In lib.php, comment out lines 22 and 40 That's it! However, this second solution doesn't solve the grade items already present in your courses set up before you comment out these lines. You will have to use the first solution for these.

The students bonus points are accrued throughout the semester, and, again, I don't want them to be part of the "denominator" when calculating the grade. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: extra credit
ResponsesInList.Text: Act as extra credit (ONLY) When the "Sum of grades" aggregation strategy is used, a grade item can act as Extra credit for the category. This means that the grade item's maximum grade will not be added to the category total's maximum grade, but the item's grade will. Following is an example: Item 1 is graded 0-100 Item 2 is graded 0-75 Item 1 has the "Act as extra credit" checkbox ticked, Item 2 doesn't. Both items belong to Category 1, which has "Sum of grades" as its aggregation strategy Category 1's total will be graded 0-75 A student gets graded 20 on Item 1 and 70 on Item 2 The student's total for Category 1 will be 75/75 (20+70 = 90 but Item 1 only acts as extra credit, so it brings the total to its maximum) So if I understand correctly, you can set up a category for your EC, choose the "sum of grades" aggregation method, then you would add EC items there and include this category in your overall course grade aggregation. Apparently, it's still not able to simply give more points than the total points possible (no giving 12/10 on an individual assignment, for example), but you can put in additional items in the EC category where you can put in the extra points. So if you had an Assignment #1 worth 10 points, you could also add an item in the EC category called Assignment #1 EC - and you could give EC there. As I understand LSU has designed a gradebook that would allow simply giving more points than the total allowed, as well as a few other possibilities, but it's not part of the core Moodle gradebook at this point. Best, clark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades displayed by group
ResponsesInList.Text: In any given situation a user will actually have multiple roles active. You inherit permissions from multiple roles at many contexts. If you can get the needed behavior with Not Set, it interacts better with these inherited permissions than a Prevent. If you use Prevent in a role, it can "block" a user from getting an Allow value in another role. A good illustration of this is too look at the permissions on the default built-in roles. I think other than guest none of the default roles use Prevent.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why can I not update grades
ResponsesInList.Text: What do you mean "they can't be changed"? Are you trying to change the grades from the assignment side or using the gradebook? If you change assignment-related grades using the gradebook, your changes will override the assignment module and prevent it from making further changes. The cream colour in your screenshot is used to show grades that have thus been "overridden" through the gradebook. The best solution is if you grade ONLY in the gradebook OR only in the assignment module, but not both. If you decide to grade using the assignment module, you will need to remove the "overridden" state of each overridden grade, by editing this grade in the gradebook. (See this documentation page for more info).

ResponsesInList.Title: using scales
ResponsesInList.Text: a question came up and I'm not able to answer it - I hope you guys can help... Is there a way to assign letter grades or percentages to scales so these grades can be aggregated in the category total? thanks martina

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using scales
ResponsesInList.Text: Martina, Percentages and letter grades are only display options , they have no effect whatsoever on calculations and aggregation. When you use a scale value, the values are stored as integers internally, and it is these values that are used for aggregation, so they will be included in the category total. These scale values can then be displayed in a variety of ways, including as a percentage of the maximum or as a letter grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using scales
ResponsesInList.Text: Nicolas, Thanks for your reply, but I have to admit I still don't really get it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using scales
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes I understand. This will depend on the aggregation strategy you choose for the category in which you put your grade item (if you haven't set up categories, it is the course category's aggregation strategy to which I'm referring). These aggregation methods are described in this documentation . For some of them, the value you attach (in your mind) to different values isn't relevant, what matters is the minimum value, the maximum value and the grade value. For example, if you have 5 items in your scale: 1. Appalling 2. Passable 3. Good 4. Very good 5. Perfect Then giving a grade of 4 (very good) is equivalent to 80% of the maximum grade, and it is this ratio (0.8) which will be used in aggregating the total score. The main restriction of scale values is that you cannot give arbitrary values to each scale value. You can't give 1 (appalling) a value of 0% while giving 2 (passable) a value of 40%.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Showing total points earned to certain point in semester
ResponsesInList.Text: Vicki, We have done the following to accomplish what I think you are asking for. You need to change the aggregation method to Simple Weighted Mean of grades (not sum of grades) and check the "Aggregate only non-empty grades".  When you do this the grade book total will only include columns with a grade entry. (teachers will have to issue a "0" and not leave it blank if a student earns a "0"). If you have categories in your class you will need to set the class total to weighted mean of grades and each category to simple weighted.  If you lose your totals you know you missed a category. Hope this helps. Bryce

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display score on gradebook don't count toward grade
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, Here's what I would do: Click on "Grades" in the administration block of your course. Click on "Choose an action" in the top left corner. From the drop-down menu select "Categories and Items " (under Edit ). At the bottom of the page click on "Add Category" Enter a name for the category e.g. "Term time Quizzes". Ignore the other settings & Save Changes Now you need to edit the "Category Total" grade item. (See my previous post on grade categories) Set the Grade type to "None" & Save Changes. Now you need to assign this new grade category to each quiz. You can do that by using the up down arrows on the Edit categories and items screen (step 3) or by going to each quiz and editing it's grade category. The grades will now appear on the student's reports but will not be included in the final grade. Did you have any trouble with Helen's method?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook Terms
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Casey, You're welcome. I use simple mean of grades for all my grade categories. You can set the maximum grade of each quiz (45), assignment (45)& participation (10) category total according to your desired weighting. I attach a screen-shot of where I would make what changes. You could try using formulas instead of my method. You have to give each grade item an ID number and then use a formula to calculate your desired result. To use formulas: 1. Click on the Calculator icon next to the category total of the item you want to change in the Categories and Item screen. 2. Give each grade item an ID number 3. At the bottom of the screen click on "Add id numbers" 4. Use the ID numbers you created to enter a formula in the Calculation area of the same screen and click save changes. Here are a couple of simple formulas you could use: (copied from the help file) average ( [[item1 ]], [[item2 ]]...): Returns the average of a sample sum ( [[item1 ]], [[item2 ]]...): Returns the sum of all arguments Hope this helps

Using Moddle 1.9 My students upload finished essays using the simple upload functionality in the course. Teachers then need to download the essays and grade them offline and then re-upload them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading and uploading results.
ResponsesInList.Text: For this functionality, your teachers will want to use the Advanced uploading of files assignment type. The upload a single file assignment does not offer a simple solution for returning a file to the student. For more information on the Advanced Upload type see http://docs.moodle.org/en/Advanced_uploading_of_files_assignment . If your teachers already have submissions to assess in the simple upload assignment type, then the best option might be to link to the graded essays through the HTML editor in the feedback area on each submission. If you need additional guidance on how to do this, let me know. Then, make sure to change all future assignments to the Advanced type to make the grading process easier on upcoming assignments.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.9 bonus points
ResponsesInList.Text: Nicolas, Here is my problem relative to the gradebook. I wanted to create an item called "Bonus" and add a maximum of .6 to those who earned a bonus. So, someone could actually end up with 100.6 overall points. But Moodle wants to always convert this to a percent, so someone who did not get bonus might end up with 100 points (a perfect 100%), but Moodle wants to calculate this person's grade as 100/100.6, or 99.4%. This .6% difference could drop some students into a lower grade category, since the letter grades are always based upon percentages, not points. I have looked for a fix and tried numerous things, but have not been able to get this to work. Any ideas would be appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.9 bonus points
ResponsesInList.Text: It really depends on what aggregration strategy you want to use. From our experiences only sum of grades works with bonus points, and it does work well. If you want a percentage for the category you can edit the category item to make it show out of 100 points (100 as maximum) and moodle will show this correctly. The only thing you need to do is create your 'bonus' item as out of the amount of points required to make up the extra 0.6%. Extra credits do NOT work with percentage based aggregations at this point in time as far as I have been able to tell. hope this helps. It is not a solution... I think there are LOT of people that would like extra credits to work 'out of the box' with percentage based aggregations. Lael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades still visible after set to hide
ResponsesInList.Text: I have not found a way to keep points from appearing when/if the student accesses the individual assignment area; irrespective if the settings for "Grades" is NO and from the Gradebook, the assignment is toggled to invisible. An alternative (with some limitations) is to do what you are doing BUT, rather than entering points(scores) in the assignment window, enter them in an external spreadsheet - this also will allow you to return to assignments and revise/re-evaluate (comments AND points) UNTIL you are ready to release [allow students to see "comments" and "points" assigned]. When ready to finalize, return to the "allow quick grading" window and enter the points earned from the spreadsheet to each student and make visible both the "Grades" setting AND the "Assignment" from the "Gradebook" - now when students access "Grades" or "Assignment" area, they will see both points and comments. If you UNCHECK "Send notification emails" your other objective will be achieved during the actual grading/comment phase. IF you follow the above alternative , you can check the "notification" box AFTER entering all scores and then students will receive the usual email alert. Regards.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do grades aggregate from child courses into meta courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Except for the enrollment feature, metacourses and their child courses function as two entirely separate courses. So, to answer your question, grades are not automatically transferred between metacourses and child courses. If you needed to enter the grades from the child courses into the metacourse, you could periodically export the grades from the child course and then import them into the gradebook in the metacourse.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook assignment returns?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1000 Gradepoint Question
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a question that several of us asked in this our first semester using Moodle (v. 1.9). Here are some quick directions. If you wish to simply add the grades, do the following. Go to "Grades" in the "Administration" section of your course, then from the drop-down menu labelled "Choose an action" in the resulting window, select "Edit/Categories and items." Then in the new window, click the edit icon by the course title. In the resulting window, change "Aggregation" to "Sum of grades." You may also wish to change the maximum value to something other than 100 so that the sum is not limited to 100. Richard Bowman

ResponsesInList.Text: The update activity page refers to the activity module to which this grade item is linked. Currently, grade items that are linked to an activity module have several settings only changeable from within the activity module's interface. Maximum grade is one of them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook Exhaustion
ResponsesInList.Text: There are a couple of ways of achieving this, depending on what you want to achieve. Let me highlight each briefly here: Set up the course to aggregate only non-empty grades: assignments not yet graded will not affect the course total. Also, optionally, you may want to hide these new assignments from students. Create a category with "Grade type" set to "None", and put each new assignment inside of it. None of its results, graded or not, will affect the course total. You can also hide the entire category from students. I tend to prefer the second option, it requires less work in the long run. There is only one tricky part: where to find the "Grade type" setting. Take a look at the screenshot to see where it is.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with including both letter grades and numeric grades in a category total
ResponsesInList.Text: Edwinna, You do not enter grades as Letters. You enter them as raw grades (delimited by the item's minimum and maximum grades), then they are converted in grade letters for display purposes only . The grades are not stored as letters in the database . When you edit grade letters, you only specify the letter grade's lower boundary . The lower boundary is always set to the next letter's (upward) lower boundary, minus 0.01.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Outcomes and criterion based assessment. Help!
ResponsesInList.Text: To clear things up about letter grades in the 1.9 gradebook: Grades are edited in one of 3 formats by teachers/staff, in the grader report: Values, delimited by min and max grade Scale Text These grades can then be displayed in several ways to the students: Raw grade: as the teacher entered it Percentage: in relation to min and max grade, curved to 0-100 Letter: Automatically display a letter depending on which range the raw grade falls into The display of the grades does not affect their raw value (the value stored in the database ). So, if you want your grades to appear as letters for your students, you do not need to use a scale. You just leave the grade type as "Value" and change the grade display type to "Letter", either in your individual grade items or for the entire course. See the grade display type documentation for more info. You can also define site-wide or per-course the ranges of grades associated with your grade letters, and even rename the letters. See the grade letter documentation .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: fixing the mess I am in
ResponsesInList.Text: Tim, You are correct about quiz. It doesn't matter how many questions you put, or how much their value is, what matters is the "maximum grade" setting. The value of each question acts as a weight towards the end result, which will be a adjusted to this maximum grade. For example, if you have 10 questions of which the max values total 50, but you set your maximum grade for this quiz to 100, if a student answers everything correctly he will get 100, which is the grade that will appear in the gradebook. You are asking where the weight setting is... It's in the screenshot you just attached, the very last item at the bottom: Item weight. It is not called "Parent weight". It's under the parent category heading because it depends on the parent category. As I said previously, you need to set this to whatever you want as long as it is consistent between the items. For example, if you want to use 22 for the first item, you shouldn't put 0.35 for the second, but 35. The weights are only meaningful as far as they relate one grade item to the other within the context of the parent category. My advice is not to set up any additional category, but simply to keep the course category as the only one, and set its aggregation to "Weighted mean of grades". You can then set each assignment to the weight you want, as well as the quiz.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I don't want to count one one of category grades in the course total
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Becky, You can exclude a particular category from the course total by adding a grade calculation for your course total, which adds each of your category totals except the one you wish to exclude, for example 
```text
=sum(
item1
,
item2
,
item3
)
```
 where item1, item2 and item3 are the ID numbers for the category totals you wish to include. Please see Grade calculations for further details.

ResponsesInList.Title: student TA's

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: student TA's
ResponsesInList.Text: You will need to create a new offline assignment activity for each homework you want to grade, and give your TAs permission to grade the activity outside the gradebook (Create overrides in your activity for the TA role). Your TAs will then be able to grade all course participants, but will still be able to see only their own grades in the gradebook.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: student TA's
ResponsesInList.Text: You cannot show/hide different grade items in the same course based on roles. The only way to achieve your result is to let your TAs view the grades as they are stored in the assignment interface (offline assignments).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mixing Scales

ResponsesInList.Title: Really Disappointed with Gradebook 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: I am a HUGE Moodle fan, user, and evangelist. So it is with genuine regret that I have concluded--after many hours of reading this forum and sincerely trying to make Gradebook 1.9 work--that I am giving up and moving over to engrade as my on line gradebook. I was really looking forward to many of the promised and discussed features of the new gradebook. I used the 1.6 Gradebook all last year and, though it had some serious limitations from my perspective, it was intuitive enough to set up and use that I learned to live with its limitations for the convenience of automatic entry of grades after assignment evaluation. I am speaking from the perspective of a K-12 teacher who regularly needs to print out notices for students of late work, attendence records, and student centered summaries of all grades for a semester organized by category for the purpose of sharing with parents at conferences or using as a reference for twice yearly narrative comments. None of these features are offered--so far as I can tell--on 1.9. But I could have lived without them if only I could have found a single page to set up the parameters and preferences for the overall gradebook at the course level. Instead of offering me a centralized interface, 1.9 has dispersed all these features over several pages and has not offered a clear, coherent, intuitive interface that "amateur" Moodle users could use easily and without repeated explanations and troubleshooting. I know that if I find a Moodle feature confusing, then there is NO WAY my technophobic colleagues will persevere. So--to those of you who are involved with designing the Gradebook for Moodle, I suggest you take a serious look at engrade or Gradekeeper to see how a teacher-friendly interface is constructed and how a spreadsheet can be made easy for ordinary users to grasp and work with.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Really Disappointed with Gradebook 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, Thanks for the links to engrade and gradekeeper. They look like they could be useful (providing they don't have any software patents!) I think pretty much everyone agrees we can improve the interfaces in the gradebook. What 1.9 brought was a really good structural foundation (all the modules report their grades consistently, and all the interfaces are now plugins so any developer can create new interfaces) plus some initial interfaces that make all the requested features *possible* for almost any educational sector. Creating intuitive user interfaces is really hard work, much harder than it looks. The job of the user community now is to help the developers improve the default user interfaces by coming up with some consensus on the changes that are required. Helen and Nicolas are already engaged with collecting and studying feedback about the Gradebook for Moodle 2.0 ( see this discussion ) to try and formulate a Gradebook roadmap, so please help with specific suggestions and voting on your favourite issues in the tracker. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with custom scaling
ResponsesInList.Text: You should never get a screen that just says 'error' -- at the very least it should tell you what went wrong. Please provide a screenshot of what you put in and I will try to reproduce this problem. Assuming you're using Windows, to make a screenshot first get the problem on screen and then press the 'print screen' button (might be labeled 'prt sc' or 'ptsrc' or similar; on a laptop you might need to press the 'function' key too). Then open 'paint' or any graphics program you're used to, and 'paste' the image in. Save it, and then use the 'attach' button when writing your reply to this post. There are plenty of guides on the internet if you get lost -- just Google for 'print screen' or 'make screenshot'. For the second part, the 1.9 gradebook allows you to 'override' grades that have been submitted by individual modules. What that means to you is that you can mark students' submissions by going to 'grades' on the module page, and then pressing 'turn editing on'. The screen becomes very full of edit buttons, but you can ignore most of them and edit students' grades individually. The grade then appears in a different colour to the others (because it's been overridden, rather than marked in the usual way), and there are other disadvantages to doing it like this, but it does allow fractional grades. Hope this is useful. Tom

The second is that it doesn't do any validation. If you put in a mark of 101 out of 100, it will swallow it (and indeed remember it), but it will appear as 100% in other views. If you put in text, it will just set the grade to zero. I hope this does what you want it to do! Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weighting Grades & Aggregate Only Non Empty Grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Aggregate only non empty grades certainly works for mean of grades (that is the average of percentages), simple weighted mean of grades (that is average of points), and Weighted mean of grades.  Sum of grades would work the same whether you counted missing grades as zero or not. Make sure you go through this tutorial as it shows the correct computations using Aggregate only non-empty grades. http://docs.moodle.org/en/Gradebook_1.9_Tutorial But the short of it is that you should not have to put items into a zero weighted category.  They are not factored into the grade until a grade is assigned (which could be zero or any other acceptable value). --Gary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 3 quick questions on 1.9 gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Just be aware that this release of the gradebook is focused almost entirely on functionality. There is no dependency on Javascript , and consequently, no AJAX layer. This means that every action requires a page reload. The reason for this is accessibility . Once this phase of development is over, and the gradebook is usable by all, we can focus on improving the interface by adding an AJAX layer, which will speed things up considerably and make the interface much more intuitive. For example, quick grading will be replaced by a system in which clicking on a grade will turn it into a form element, letting you change it, and as soon as you click out of it, the grade will be updated in the database , without the need for a page reload. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Switching from GBv2 to 1.9's Gradebook - how goes it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Regarding item #1, the following steps should bring a more satisfactory resolution than have everybody change their own grades: Perform the following sql query: UPDATE `mdl_grade_category` set aggregation = 11 where aggregation = 10. This will replace all grade categories set to "Weighted Mean of Grades" with "Simple Weighted Mean of Grade". Perform the following sql query: UPDATE `mdl_grade_category` set aggregation = 11 where aggregation = 9. This will replace all grade categories set to "Mean of Grades" with "Simple Weighted Mean of Grade". Go into Site Administration->Grades->General Settings Toggle the "Include Scales in Aggregation" checkbox on or off Save Changes. It will take a while for grades in the system to recalculate. Toggle the "Include Scales in Aggregation" back to its original position before step 3 Save Changes again. You should now see category totals and course totals for those categories messed up by this.

ResponsesInList.Text: Warning: This post is not going to be about php code! I am offering a course to faculty on how to use Moodle and I absolutely do not like the new gradebook in 1.9. It just will not do what I want, give simple list of points given. This is especially hard because 50% of the final points is for the student's creation of a course shell. I am constantly getting irate or whinging emails from students "why is my grade so and so?" and I can't blame them. It all seems so random and needlessly complicated. I like the old gradebook better. Is there an alternative? I am just one person here, so I can't call on i.t. to make me a new grade book to drop in.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook headaches
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, there is no question that the new gradebook is a lot more painful to use. It has some compensations. I like the ability to set it up so that an empty grade doesn't count against a student, so the students can see their updated score as soon as I grade it, without penalizing those I haven't gotten to yet. On the other hand, extra credit has been scuttled. I have some hope that the "simple grader" discussed here may address some of this... To set up an assignment that is 50% of the course total, create a category that has 50% weight. Go to Grades->Edit->Categories and items (that means go to grades and then select the drop down to find "Categories and items.") Once you have created the category, go back to the tree and select the "edit" icon for the category you just created. Under "parent" you can now set the weight as a percentage. Now find the assignment that you want to be worth 50%. The easiest way to do this is load the assignment itself and click on "Update this assignment." Down near the bottom there is a drop down labeled "Grade category." Use this to place that assignment in the new category you just created. You may want to create another category (or more) for the other assignments, and make them all sum up to 100%. Place the other assignments in the other category. There, wasn't that easy? :/

And even for a quiz that is going to close, having it "hidden" in the gradebook (rather than just without a score) is very confusing. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category Totals Won't display
ResponsesInList.Text: I had this problem when I first tried converting to Moodle 1.9 from 1.8. In my case, there were no category totals because the categories were set to "Weighted mean" but the weighting factors defaulted to zero. I expect this situation should only arise when you have converted from 1.8 to 1.9. Bob Puffer set me on the path to fix my problem. I used PhpMyAdmin to set everything but the course grade to "Simple weighted mean" (which was the way it was done in version 1.8). Then I had to force re-calculation of the category totals. Here is the sequence I used (copied from the documentation for Gradebookplus): First, set all assignments and categories that are NOT the course grade to "Simple Weighted Mean of Grade" with the MySQL command below: UPDATE mdl_grade_categories SET aggregation = 11 WHERE depth != 1; It is now necessary to force Moodle to reaggregate grades. This can be accomplished with the following steps: Go into Site Administration->Grades->General Settings Toggle the "Include Scales in Aggregation" checkbox on or off Save Changes. It will take a while for grades in the system to recalculate. Toggle the "Include Scales in Aggregation" back to its original position before step 3 Save Changes again. I wouldn't do this if teachers have already been working in courses in version 1.9 because they may not take kindly to having you change the way they have their gradebook set up. Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Giving scores for forum posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alexis, To be honest, it sounds like you're pushing uphill a bit trying to do this with a forum activity, for the following reasons: YES, you can allow multiple posts, YES, you can use a summation of marks to display in the Gradebook, YES, you can set each post to be worth a maximum of 50 points, BUT then you start to hit up against the problem of the summation of marks blowing out the total to more than the maximum individual mark (and to be honest I'm struggling to see how anyone could use the summation of marks without this happening). Without doing some tweaking you can't set the max mark in the activity itself to be more than 100, so maybe try the following: Set the 'grade' setting in the forum to 75 Set the 'aggregate type' to 'sum of ratings' Mark each post out of 25 Bingo - you've got a summed total which truncates at 75 In the Gradebook, use a multiplier of 2 for that gradebook item (assuming you are using Moodle v1.9.x) which will then translate it to 150. Clunky, but it should work I think... Note that this won't 'guarantee' that students will make three posts, if you want to do that then you might be better off considering a Database activity, where you can set more things like that than in a forum. Hope this helps,

ResponsesInList.Title: Some gradebook observations
ResponsesInList.Text: I am the Moodle software development project manager at Louisiana State University and we have some of the same needs that I see posted on these boards. One of the MANY development projects we are working on (almost done) is creating an alternative drop-in replacement for the current gradebook. We've gone a long way to simplifying the Moodle 1.9 grade book for mere mortals to use, but we've run into a few minor snags and a few major "What were they thinking" snags. Sum aggregation method is entirely broken in its current form Drop lowest/Keep highest does not work in Sum, even though they are still shown and no one on tracker cares. We've eliminated keep highest/drop lowest for sum as it does not make sense from a mathematical perspective anyway and fixed the problem if you've set drop/keep in another aggregation method, then switched to sum. Exclude does not work in Sum, even though it is still allowed and no one on tracker cares. We removed the ability to exclude grades when using sum and fixed the problem if you've excluded something in another aggregation method, then switched to sum. The aggregation coefficient being 0 for sum majorly screws things up when switching between Weighted Mean and Sum. Making the default aggregation coefficient 0 makes no sense at all for sum to be calculated. We made the aggregation coefficient 1 for sum's default and 0 for extra credit, this way we can use extra credit on weighted mean as well. Category totals do not update totals when switching from Sum to Weighted Mean. We've fixed this in our grade book as well. Way too many aggregation methods There needs to be an administrative way to hide aggregation methods (and other things) from instructors. (PLEASE!) Our grade book only includes Weighted mean and Sum as our instructors got confused with too many options. We are debating the inclusion of simple weighted mean as well. Calculations work great, except no-one but our developers seem to understand them. We removed calculations! To cope with this huge change, we added extra credit in Weighted Mean We fixed sum and also fixed the nastiness that occurs when changing from one aggregation method to another We made the default of weighted mean to be mean (all aggregation coefficients default to 1) We made sum's default aggregation coefficient to be 1 We made sum extra credit aggregation coefficient to be 0 We made weighted mean's extra credit aggregation coefficient to be 0 We allow instructors to give points above the maximum We allow percentages to go above 100% Grader Report UI needs help

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Some gradebook observations
ResponsesInList.Text: aggregationcoef is set to 0 in Moodle core. This means that all new grade items have a aggregation coefficient of 0, and as such, they have a weight of 0 in things like weighted mean. When extra credit was introduced for sum, they chose to change aggregationcoef to 1 when someone selected the extra credit checkbox that only is a checkbox once in a while. This means that sum graded items could have an aggregation coefficient (weight) of greater than 0, and up to but not including 1; or larger than 1 to infinity. If you wanted it to make the aggregation coefficient 1 for a sum item to make it count for its displayed value, you had to set it back to 0, which was not so intuitive. They hid this somewhat well from end users, but we wanted extra credit everywhere and having to avoid 1 and replace 0 for 1 everywhere did not make sense to us, hence the change. My explanation for your next question also brings this up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Some gradebook observations
ResponsesInList.Text: Our default implementation of weighted mean is EXACTLY the same as mean. Because our aggregation coefficient is 1 (weight = 1) the agg method behaves exactly like mean. Only when changes are made to the weights, does the system behave like a weighted mean system. Simple weighted mean is not so simple all the time. It can be explained mathematically two different ways. The first way is the total of points divided by the total of possible points (this method assumes the minimum grade is 0). This is the simpler way to figure this out and is as follows: A1 90/100 Minimum grade 0 A2 70/80 Minimum grade 0 A3 60/90 Minimum grade 0 Category max 100: ((90+70+60)/(100+80+90)) = 220/270 = .8148 = 81.48/100 = 81.48% The old method dealt with minimum grades (which we've removed as well to simplify things) which confused matters and forced you to use the alternate method of calculating SWM grades which is a PITA. The more complicated way is as follows and accounts for minimum grades greater than 0: A1 90/100 Minimum grade 20 A2 70/80 Minimum grade 10 A3 60/90 Minimum grade 30 Category max 100: ((A1-A1_grade_min)+(A2-A2_grade_min)+(A3-A3_grade_min))/((A1_grade_max-A1_grade_min)+( A2_grade_max-A2_grade_min)+( A3_grade_max-A3_grade_min))*100 = ((90-20)+(70-10)+(60-30))/((100-20)+(80-10)+(90-30)) = ((70+60+30)/(80+70+60)) = (160/210) = .7619 = 76.19/100 = 76.19% Uggh... We have decided not to confuse the hell out of people and removed minimum from ALL aggregation methods as it makes weighted mean MUCH more fun too. Weighted mean is not as simple as Simple weighted mean, hence the name. Thankfully Weighted mean can only be explained mathematically one way (probably shooting myself in the foot by saying that here). A1 90/100 Minimum grade 0 weight 1 A2 70/80 Minimum grade 0 weight 2 A3 60/90 Minimum grade 0 weight 3 Category max 100: (((((A1-grade_min)/(A1_grade_max-A1_grade_min))*1)+((70/80)*2)+((60/90)*3))/(1+2+3)) = ((.9*1)+(.875*2)+(.6666667*3))/6 = 4.65/6 = .775 = 77.5/100 = 77.5% ((((90/100)*1)+((70/80)*2)+((60/90)*3))/(1+2+3)) = ((.9*1)+(.875*2)+(.6666667*3))/6 = 4.65/6 = .775 = 77.5/100 = 77.5% The Extra Credit points are added to the category total for all 3 aggregation methods and will not cause any other effect on the category grades.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Some gradebook observations
ResponsesInList.Text: Sum calculates the grade out of the total points allowed, (a+b+c) then to get a percent it divides by (a_max+b_max+c_max) looking a whole lot like simple weighted mean. Simple Weighted Mean does the same thing, but will then scale that grade so it is out of the total category points (which is editable in SWM and not in Sum). This is VERY useful for weighting categories, using SWM inside other aggregation methods (like Sum). We originally removed it, but we re-added it after complaints from instructors arose. We will submit our Simple Grade Book suite for inclusion in contrib within the next few days.
